item.title: What is Calcium Carbonate and Its Applications in Plastics Industry
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3) is one of the most widely used mineral fillers in modern industries, playing a crucial role in manufacturing plastics, paper, paints, rubber, and construction materials. In particular, within the plastic and packaging sectors, Calcium Carbonate has become an essential ingredient, helping manufacturers reduce costs, enhance product performance, and promote sustainable production. 1. What is Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3)? Canxi Cacbonat (CaCO3) is a chemical compound that is common in nature. It is a natural neutralizer and plays an important role in environmental balance. CaCO3 is a salt of calcium and carbonic acid, which exists mainly in white solid and powder form.  Calcium Carbonate is an inorganic compound found naturally in rocks such as limestone, marble, and chalk. It appears as a fine white powder, insoluble in water, odorless, non-toxic, and chemically stable.  Thanks to its high whiteness, purity, and stable dispersion, CaCO3 is considered a versatile additive used across industries that require cost optimization and improved material performance. 2. Main Types of Calcium Carbonate There are two main industrial forms of CaCO3:  GCC (Ground Calcium Carbonate): Made by grinding natural limestone. Economical and suitable for general plastic applications.  PCC (Precipitated Calcium Carbonate): Produced through a controlled chemical process, offering finer, purer, and brighter particles, often used in high-end applications such as coatings, pharmaceuticals and technical plastics. 3. General Industrial Applications Because of its abundance and excellent properties, Calcium Carbonate is used in many industries: 
Industry Application of CaCO₃ Main Benefits
Plastics Functional filler Improves stiffness, surface gloss, reduces cost
Paper Coating/filler Enhances brightness, opacity, smoothness
Paints Pigment extender Improves coverage, stability
Rubber Reinforcing agent Increases hardness and strength
Construction Additive Reduces cost, improves strength
4. The Role of Calcium Carbonate in Plastics – Filler Masterbatch In plastics, Calcium Carbonate is mostly used as filler masterbatch – a compound of CaCO₃, polymer (PP/PE), and additives, processed into pellets. These pellets are mixed with virgin resin during extrusion, molding or blowing film.  Benefits of Using Calcium Carbonate in Plastics
  • Cost Reduction Calcium Carbonate replaces part of the virgin polymer, helping manufacturers significantly reduce material costs while maintaining product performance.
  • Improved Mechanical Strength  Calcium Carbonate increases stiffness, dimensional stability, and tensile strength, making products more durable and resistant to deformation.
  • Enhanced Processability  Calcium Carbonate improves heat conductivity, shortens cooling time, and allows faster molding cycles in extrusion or injection processes.
  • Environmental Sustainability Using filler masterbatch reduces dependency on petroleum-based polymers, lowering carbon footprint and promoting eco-friendly production.

5. Typical Applications of CaCO3 Filler Masterbatch

  • Packaging films and shopping bags
  • PP woven sacks
  • PP non-woven fabric
  • Injection molding
  • Sheets, pipes, profiles
CaCO₃ helps in optimally balancing the price – stability of the product. 

6. Mascom Global – Reliable Partner in Filler Masterbatch Production From CaCO3

Among Vietnam’s leading filler masterbatch manufacturers, Mascom Global stands out with its large capacity, advanced technology and high-quality standards.  Highlights: 
  • Production Capacity: over 400,000 tons/year – top leading manufacturer in Viet Nam.
  • Advanced-technology Equipment: ensures high dispersion and stable quality.
  • Experienced Team: passionate, dedicated, and technically strong.
  • Global Market: exported to over 70 countries worldwide.
Mascom Global is not only a manufacturer but a trusted partner helping customers enhance product quality and competitiveness.

7. Future Outlook

As the plastic industry moves toward sustainability, the role of Calcium Carbonate will become even more important.

Future innovations such as nano CaCO₃ and surface treatment technologies will continue improving filler performance and open new applications.

Conclusion

Calcium Carbonate (CaCO₃) has evolved from a simple mineral into a strategic material supporting global manufacturing. In plastics, especially through Filler Masterbatch, it provides the perfect balance of cost, performance, and sustainability. With technology, capacity, and passion, Mascom Global proudly contributes to elevating Vietnam’s position in the global plastics industry.

item.title: Why You Should Buy PVC Compound from Trusted Manufacturers
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In the world of technical plastics and cable production, the PVC compound you choose is the foundation of your final product’s performance. Not every PVC compound is created equal. When you search to "buy PVC compound", you are strategically choosing quality, consistency, and long-term reliability. Partnering with a trusted manufacturer like Mascom Global ensures your materials meet the highest global standards, minimizing costly production risks. Discover the non-negotiable advantages a leading supplier offers, from stable quality and international compliance to custom formulas tailored exactly to your needs.

The Pillars of Quality: What Trusted Suppliers Offer 

Choosing a leading, specialized manufacturer means securing several critical advantages that small-scale or non-specialized suppliers often cannot match, forming the foundation of a robust B2B relationship. [caption id="attachment_1795" align="aligncenter" width="1080"] The Pillars of Quality: What Trusted Suppliers Offer[/caption]

1. Stable Quality and Batch-to-Batch Consistency 

In high-volume manufacturing, especially in precision fields like cable jacketing or extrusion, even minor deviation between material batches can cause catastrophic downtime and product failure. Trusted manufacturers invest heavily in state-of-the-art compounding equipment and strictly controlled mixing procedures to guarantee:
  • Uniformity: Every pellet in every shipment is subjected to high-level quality assurance, ensuring an identical molecular structure, consistent melt flow index, and reliable extrusion performance across long production runs.
  • Predictability: Your operators and machines can rely on the material behaving the exact same way, every time, reducing the need for constant line adjustments and minimizing material waste. This reliability is paramount to maintaining tight production schedules.

2. Strict Quality Control and International Compliance 

Reliable, forward-thinking suppliers prioritize international compliance and strict quality assurance (QA/QC) to protect your finished goods in demanding global markets. Mascom Global ensures:
  • Regulatory Adherence: Full compliance with critical global directives, including RoHS (Restriction of Hazardous Substances), REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals), and UL (Underwriters Laboratories) listings, which are non-negotiable for electrical, automotive, and consumer components.
  • Rigorous Testing Protocols: Compounds undergo comprehensive, in-house testing for key physical and chemical properties, including Shore A/D hardness, ultimate tensile strength, elongation at break, thermal stability (TGA), and environmental stress cracking resistance (ESCR). This proactive testing eliminates costly surprises down the line.

3. Customized Formulas for Specialized Applications 

A true partner PVC compound manufacturer acts as a technical extension of your own R&D department. They offer sophisticated customized formulations precisely tailored to the specific functional and environmental demands of your application:
  • Electrical Insulation: High dielectric strength and temperature performance ratings (e.g., 90°C, 105°C) for sensitive wire and cable jacketing.
  • Medical & Food Grade: Non-toxic, phthalate-free, and migration-resistant compounds for applications requiring strict biosecurity and purity.
  • Outdoor Resilience: Enhanced $\text{UV resistance}$, anti-fungal, and extreme weather stabilizers for outdoor construction profiles and agricultural irrigation components.
  • Safety Critical: Specialized fire-retardant (FR) and low smoke zero halogen (LSZH) grades essential for public infrastructure, mass transit, and building construction safety.

4. Reliable Supply Chain and Strong Technical Support 

Supply chain stability is the backbone of modern manufacturing. Choosing an established manufacturer mitigates your risk of unexpected production halts:

item.title: How to Choose the Right PVC Compound for Electrical Cables
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In the manufacturing of electrical cables, the performance, safety, and lifespan of the final product hinge entirely on one critical component: the PVC compound for electrical cables. This material serves as the primary insulator and protective jacketing, defining the cable’s resistance to heat, fire, moisture, and abrasion. Choosing the wrong compound can lead to costly product failures, regulatory non-compliance, and catastrophic safety issues. When sourcing this vital material, procurement managers and R&D teams must move beyond price and focus on technical specifications and supplier reliability. At Mascom Global, we engineer PVC compounds designed for excellence in electrical applications, guaranteeing the integrity and durability of your cables under the toughest conditions. This guide outlines the five non-negotiable factors you must evaluate when selecting your PVC compound supplier.

How to Choose the Right PVC Compound for Electrical Cables

The complexity of electrical environments—ranging from household wiring to heavy-duty industrial infrastructure—requires specialized material properties. Here are the crucial elements determining the quality of your cable compound:

1. Electrical Resistance and Insulation Strength

The primary function of a PVC compound for electrical cables is insulation. This material must possess high dielectric strength to prevent current leakage and maintain circuit integrity. [caption id="attachment_1825" align="aligncenter" width="675"] Electrical Resistance and Insulation Strength[/caption]
  • Dielectric Strength: This measures the maximum electric field the material can withstand without electrical breakdown. For safety and compliance, your compound must maintain high dielectric properties even under mechanical stress or elevated temperatures.
  • Volume Resistivity: This determines how strongly the material resists electrical current flow. A high resistivity compound ensures minimal energy loss and efficient power transmission. Always request a compound with proven stability in its insulation characteristics across its operational lifespan.

2. Thermal Stability and Temperature Rating 

Electrical cables generate heat under load, and external environmental temperatures vary widely. The PVC compound must remain stable without degrading or melting. [caption id="attachment_1826" align="aligncenter" width="675"] Thermal Stability and Temperature Rating[/caption]
  • Temperature Rating: Cables are typically rated for 70°C, 90°C, or even 105°C continuous use. Ensure your supplier can verify the compound’s performance at the required operational temperature. Lower-quality compounds can soften and deform, compromising insulation when overheated.
  • Thermal Aging: Over time, heat exposure causes materials to age. A high-quality compound includes effective heat stabilizers to maintain its physical and electrical integrity over the cable’s intended service life, often decades.

3. Flame Retardancy and Safety Compliance 

In any application, especially construction and public transport, fire safety is paramount. The PVC compound is the first defense against flame propagation. [caption id="attachment_1827" align="aligncenter" width="675"] Flame Retardancy and Safety Compliance[/caption]
  • Flame Retardancy (FR): Standard electrical PVC compounds contain additives that cause them to self-extinguish when the flame source is removed. Ensure the compound meets standards like UL VW-1 or IEC 60332.
  • Low Smoke Zero Halogen (LSZH): For enclosed spaces like tunnels, aircraft, and high-rise buildings, LSZH compounds are required. These specialized materials drastically reduce the emission of opaque smoke and toxic halogen gases during a fire, saving lives and protecting sensitive equipment.

4. Processability and Extrusion Compatibility 

A technically superior compound is worthless if it cannot be processed efficiently on your equipment. Manufacturers must guarantee seamless compatibility with high-speed cable extrusion lines. [caption id="attachment_1828" align="aligncenter" width="675"] Processability and Extrusion Compatibility[/caption]
  • Melt Flow Index (MFI): The compound must exhibit a consistent and optimized MFI to ensure smooth extrusion without pressure variations, voids, or die drool. Batch-to-batch consistency is critical here; deviations cause costly machine adjustments and scrap material.
  • Surface Finish: The compound must yield a smooth, flawless surface finish on the jacketing, essential for both aesthetic quality and reducing friction during cable pulling and installation.

5. Environmental Compliance (RoHS, REACH) 

In today's global market, environmental regulations dictate trade. Non-compliant materials expose your company to legal risks and block market access.
  • RoHS (Restriction of Hazardous Substances): This directive restricts the use of specific hazardous materials (like lead and cadmium) in electrical products. Your supplier must provide certified, fully RoHS-compliant PVC compounds.
  • REACH: This EU regulation addresses the manufacturing and use of chemical substances. Choosing a supplier that fully complies with REACH ensures your supply chain is stable and legally secure for export to the European Union and other regulated markets.
Learn more: PVC Compound For Wire And Cable Vietnam – Your Reliable Sourcing Choice

The Mascom Global Advantage in Cable Materials 

As a specialized supplier, Mascom Global provides materials engineered specifically for the pressures and demands of cable manufacturing. We are more than a bulk provider; we are a dedicated technical partner. [caption id="attachment_1829" align="aligncenter" width="675"] The Mascom Global Advantage in Cable Materials[/caption]

1. Guaranteed Consistency Through Advanced QA/QC 

We understand that consistency is reliability. Our compounding process is subject to multi-stage quality control, guaranteeing that every single pallet of PVC compound for electrical cables maintains identical physical and electrical properties. This predictability minimizes material waste and maximizes your production uptime.

2. Expertise in Custom Formulation 

Do you need a specific balance between flexibility (for tight bends) and hardness (for abrasion resistance)? Our R&D team can develop sophisticated, customized PVC formulas that meet complex requirements, including:
  • Extreme temperature ratings (up to 125°C).
  • High-flex compounds for robotic or winding applications.
  • Color matching for global coding standards (IEC/NEC).

3. Dedicated Technical Support and Global Logistics 

When you buy PVC compound from Mascom Global, you gain immediate access to our technical specialists. They can assist with processing optimization, solve extrusion issues, and provide all necessary technical data sheets (TDS) and safety documentation. Our global logistics network ensures prompt, reliable delivery, maintaining the integrity of your supply chain.

Partnering for Performance and Safety 

The choice of PVC compound for electrical cables is a decision that dictates safety, cost, and reputation. By prioritizing key factors—insulation strength, thermal performance, safety compliance, process compatibility, and environmental adherence—you ensure the longevity and reliability of your final product. Don't settle for generic materials. Choose a specialized partner committed to delivering high-performance, compliant, and consistent solutions. 💡 At Mascom Global, our PVC compounds for electrical applications are engineered to deliver excellent insulation and flexibility under tough conditions.

item.title: Why Sheathing PVC Compound Matters for Cable Safety
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Cables are essential for transmitting power and data, but their safety and durability hinge on the outer protection. The sheathing layer is the cable's critical first line of defense. For decades, high-quality sheathing PVC compound has been the industry benchmark, offering superior protection against environmental and mechanical stresses. Choosing the right sheathing PVC compound is not merely a material selection; it is a vital investment that guarantees a longer cable lifespan and proactively prevents product failures, ensuring enhanced operational safety and reliability.

What is Cable Sheathing and Why is it Essential?

The term "sheathing" refers to the outermost layer of a cable, which encases the insulated conductors and acts as a protective shield. Think of it as the cable's skin. If the skin is compromised, the entire organism is at risk. [caption id="attachment_1838" align="aligncenter" width="675"] What is Cable Sheathing and Why is it Essential?[/caption] The necessity of robust sheathing stems from the harsh environments in which cables often operate. They are frequently exposed to:
  • Mechanical Stress: Abrasion, crushing, impact, and bending during installation and operation.
  • Environmental Factors: UV radiation from sunlight, temperature fluctuations, and moisture (water and humidity).
  • Chemical Threats: Oils, solvents, acids, and other corrosive substances common in industrial settings.
Without an effective sheathing material, the underlying insulation layers and conductors would quickly degrade, leading to shorts, power loss, fire hazards, and complete system failure. The importance of the sheathing layer in maintaining electrical integrity and preventing safety incidents cannot be overstated. Learn more: PVC Compound For Wire And Cable Vietnam – Your Reliable Sourcing Choice

The Superiority of Sheathing PVC Compound

PVC has earned its reputation as a leading sheathing material due to its inherent versatility and cost-effectiveness. However, not all PVC compounds are created equal. High-grade sheathing PVC compounds are specially formulated to maximize their protective capabilities. [caption id="attachment_1839" align="aligncenter" width="675"] The Superiority of Sheathing PVC Compound[/caption]

1. Strong Mechanical Durability: The Armor Plate

One of the most critical roles of the sheathing layer is to provide mechanical durability. Cables, particularly in industrial settings, are constantly subjected to rough handling and physical stress.
  • Abrasion Resistance: A premium PVC compound resists wear and tear when dragged over rough surfaces, protecting the core from damage during installation.
  • Impact and Crush Resistance: It must withstand accidental impacts or pressure without rupturing, ensuring the conductors remain intact and insulated.
  • Flexibility and Smooth Processing: While being tough, the compound must also be flexible enough to allow for easy coiling, bending, and installation (a process known as smooth extrusion). This ensures the manufacturing process is efficient and the final cable is easy to handle without compromising its structure.

2. Excellent Adhesion with Insulation Layers: A Unified Defense

For maximum protection, the sheathing layer must work in perfect concert with the insulation underneath. Excellent adhesion between the sheathing and the internal insulation is crucial. Poor adhesion can lead to voids, which can trap moisture or allow the sheathing to easily peel away, exposing the delicate insulation to damage. High-quality PVC compounds are engineered to bond effectively, creating a unified, hermetically sealed defense system.

3. UV and Weather Resistance: Battling the Elements

Cables used in outdoor or exposed applications must stand up to the relentless forces of nature. UV radiation from the sun is a notorious material degrader, causing cracking, embrittlement, and discoloration over time.
  • UV Resistance: Specially formulated UV-stabilized PVC sheathing compounds ensure the cable maintains its structural integrity and mechanical properties even after prolonged exposure to sunlight. This is vital for solar power systems, external wiring, and telecommunications cables.
  • Weather Resistance (Water and Temperature): The sheathing must be impermeable to moisture and resistant to cracking across a wide temperature range, from freezing winters to scorching summers. This prevents water ingress, which can rapidly lead to electrical failures and corrosion.

4. Fire Safety Characteristics: A Crucial Safety Feature

Modern safety standards increasingly demand cables that minimize fire risk. PVC compounds can be formulated to exhibit exceptional flame-retardant properties. In the event of a fire, these compounds can self-extinguish or significantly restrict the spread of flames, thereby protecting assets and, most importantly, saving lives. This is a non-negotiable requirement for cables used in public buildings, mass transit systems, and critical infrastructure.

The Financial and Operational Impact of Choosing the Right Compound

The decision on which sheathing material to use has profound implications that extend beyond the cable’s immediate performance. [caption id="attachment_1757" align="aligncenter" width="1080"] The Financial and Operational Impact of Choosing the Right Compound[/caption]

1. Longer Cable Lifespan

A cable protected by an inferior sheathing compound will fail prematurely. This leads to costly replacement, downtime, and labor expenses. By investing in a premium sheathing PVC compound, manufacturers are effectively guaranteeing a longer cable lifespan. This means lower total cost of ownership (TCO) for the end-user and a stronger reputation for the cable manufacturer.

2. Compliance and Certification

The materials used in cable manufacturing must comply with numerous international standards (e.g., IEC, UL, VDE). A reputable compound supplier ensures their sheathing-grade PVC compounds meet the stringent requirements for durability, fire safety, and environmental resistance. This simplifies the certification process for cable manufacturers and confirms the product's safety and quality for global markets.

3. Avoiding Product Failures and Recalls

Product failures due to material degradation can result in massive financial losses from recalls, legal liabilities, and irreparable damage to a brand's reputation. Choosing a proven, high-quality sheathing compound is the single best preventative measure against these catastrophic outcomes. Choosing the right sheathing compound means longer cable lifespan and fewer product failures.

Securing Your Cable Project with Quality Sheathing

The sheathing layer is truly the unsung hero of the cable world. It is the protective shield that allows the cable to perform its vital functions under the most challenging conditions. The choice of material—specifically the sheathing PVC compound—is the foundational decision that dictates the cable's reliability, safety, and longevity. Manufacturers must partner with compound suppliers who understand the rigorous demands of the cable industry and who can provide formulations optimized for specific environments—be it a dry indoor data center, a corrosive chemical plant, or an exposed outdoor power grid. For your next cable project, don’t compromise on the protective layer. Ensure your cables are safeguarded by the best defense available. 👉 Contact Mascom Global for sheathing-grade PVC compounds and get technical samples for your next cable project.

The product is widely used in manufacturing, especially in the following industries: 
  • Plastic packaging: bags, PE and PP films
  • Plastic pipes and construction accessories: PVC, HDPE
  • Household products: basins, containers, kitchenware
  • Automotive and electronics components: machine casings, covers
Benefits of high-quality black masterbatch:

What is White Masterbatch? 

White Masterbatch is a highly concentrated mixture of Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂), polymers, and other additives — designed to deliver superior whiteness, opacity, and brightness in plastic products. It is widely used in film extrusion, injection molding, blow molding, and other plastic production, ensuring excellent dispersion, UV protection, and long-term color stability. 

Mascom Global – Trusted White Masterbatch Manufacturer from Vietnam 

At Mascom Global, we specialize in producing and exporting high-quality White Masterbatch that meets international standards. Our formulations are designed with excellent source TiO₂ and advanced carrier resins (PE & PP) to ensure: 
  • ✅ Brilliant whiteness and high opacity 
  • ✅ Excellent dispersion and consistency 
  • ✅ High Weather Fastness & Light Fastness Value 
  • ✅ Strong UV and weather resistance  
  • ✅ Smooth processing on all extrusion and molding lines 
  • ✅ Compatibility with multiple polymers (PP, PE, PS, ABS, etc.) 
With the modernest underwater pelletizer & triple-screw extrusion technology, Mascom Global White masterbatch brings outstanding features  
  • Superior pellet quality: The water-cooling process rapidly solidifies the pellets, ensuring they have a uniform size and smooth, consistent shape. This minimizes fines and dust, which is critical for color concentrates where consistent dispersion is key. 
  • High production efficiency: Underwater systems allow for continuous operation, which increases throughput and production rates compared to other methods. 
  • Versatility: This process is suitable for a wide range of polymers and is effective for producing masterbatches, including those with high pigment loads like white masterbatch. 
  • Improved product integrity: The immediate cooling in water minimizes oxidation and thermal degradation, helping to maintain the integrity of the masterbatch. 
  • Reduced need for post-processing: In many cases, the pellets are dry enough after cooling and dewatering to be used without additional drying steps, simplifying the process and saving energy. 

White Masterbatch is produced at Mascom Global factory and is applied in many industries.

With the strict quality control and competitive pricing, Mascom Global has become a trusted supplier for customers across Asia, the Middle East, Europe, and the Americas.  Our mission is to provide customers with sustainable, stable, and high-performance masterbatch solutions that enhance product quality and production efficiency.

The plastic additives industry in Vietnam has developed strongly over the past decade, becoming one of the key sectors in the supply chain for plastics, packaging, and construction. With an average annual growth rate of 10–15%, Vietnam is gradually affirming its position as one of the largest plastic additive production hubs in the country, supplying hundreds of thousands of tons of products every month to both domestic and international markets.  The expansion of consumer industries, along with the increasing demand for quality and environmental friendliness, has driven local enterprises to invest heavily in production technology and quality management systems. Among them, Mascom Global stands out as one of the young companies with exceptional growth, quickly rising to a leading position in Vietnam’s plastic additives industry. With a team of experienced engineers, modern production lines, and a sustainable development orientation, Mascom Global continues to strengthen its brand, expand its market share, and aims to become a strategic partner of major corporations both domestically and internationally. 

Additive Masterbatch - Mascom Global Factory

1. Mascom Global – Leading in Scale, Technology, and Growth

Mascom Global is recognized as one of the leading filler and additive masterbatch manufacturers in Vietnam. Despite being relatively young in the industry, Mascom has built a strong reputation through strategic investment in infrastructure, European-standard production lines, and a highly skilled technical team.  Currently, the company operates with an annual production capacity of over 300,000 tons/year, ensuring a stable and large-scale supply for both domestic and international customers. Mascom’s main product lines include Filler Masterbatch, White Masterbatch, Color Masterbatch, and Additive Masterbatch, which are widely used in the production of packaging, PP/PE woven sacks, pipes, engineering plastics, and high-grade films.  Mascom’s products are highly regarded for their excellent dispersion, consistent color quality, and batch-to-batch stability. In addition, the company focuses on developing eco-friendly additive solutions that enhance recyclability and reduce plastic waste across the production chain.  Through continuous improvement and innovation, Mascom Global has successfully exported its products to more than 70 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia, the Middle East, and Africa, becoming one of the most reputable and competitive Vietnamese brands in the global plastic additive market. 

2. Top Plastic Additive Manufacturers in Vietnam

In addition to Mascom Global, Vietnam is home to several major enterprises that play a crucial role in the development of the plastic additive industry, helping to elevate the reputation of Vietnamese manufacturing worldwide, including: 
  • EuP – A pioneering company in filler masterbatch manufacturing, known for its large-scale production capacity and global distribution network. 
  • Mega Plast – A high-capacity manufacturer focusing on premium-quality products for export markets. 
  • Tan Dai Hung Plastic – A long-established brand recognized for its continuous technical innovation and consistent product quality. 
  • Plastika Vietnam – Equipped with European technology, specializing in additive masterbatch for packaging and high-performance plastic applications. 
Together, these companies have helped position Vietnam as a reliable and high-quality supplier of plastic additives, strengthening the country’s standing in the global plastics industry.  

Additive Masterbatch production line at Mascom Global factory

3. Vision and Development Orientation of Mascom Global 

Mascom Global aims to become a comprehensive solution provider in the plastic additive industry, not only as a manufacturer but also as a trusted partner supporting clients in formula optimization, performance enhancement, and cost efficiency.  Guided by the philosophy “Real Value Commitment”, Mascom continuously invests in innovation, sustainable development, and customer service excellence. The company is becoming a symbol of a new generation of Vietnamese enterprises — dynamic, professional, and globally oriented.  With the combination of advanced technology, an experienced team of specialists, and a long-term development strategy, Mascom Global is steadily affirming its position as a symbol of Vietnam’s manufacturing capability in the global plastic additive industry.

item.title: Black PP Masterbatch and The Production Process at Mascom Global
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
What is Black PP Masterbatch? 

Black PP Masterbatch (Black Polypropylene Masterbatch) is a type of color masterbatch produced by dispersing black pigment—most commonly Carbon Black—into a PP (Polypropylene) carrier resin together with dispersing agents and specialized additives. It is widely used across the plastics industry to provide a deep black color for end-products while enhancing the mechanical and physical properties of the material. 

Black PP Masterbatch at Mascom Global's Factory

Key features of Black PP Masterbatch include: 
  • Deep, rich black color with excellent opacity, suitable for both aesthetic and functional requirements 
  • Outstanding pigment dispersion, preventing streaks or color spots 
  • Improved mechanical strength, impact resistance, scratch resistance, and heat resistance 
  • Excellent thermal stability, ideal for injection molding, film blowing, fiber extrusion, or pipe extrusion 
  • Strong UV resistance, especially when combined with UV stabilizers 
Black PP Masterbatch is widely applied in: 
  • Industrial and consumer packaging 
  • Household goods and technical plastic products 
  • Plastic pipes, trays, and pallets 
  • Injection molding, sheet extrusion, and PP fibers 
  • Applications requiring high weather resistance 
Thanks to its strong color intensity and superior durability, Black PP Masterbatch is a preferred choice for many plastic manufacturing sectors. 

Black PP Masterbatch Production Process at Mascom Global 

As a leading brand in the masterbatch industry, Mascom Global follows an internationally standardized production process to ensure exceptional consistency and high stability across all batches of Black PP Masterbatch. 

1. Selecting high-quality Carbon Black pigments

Carbon Black is the most critical component determining the performance of black masterbatch. At Mascom Global, the factory uses Carbon Black grades with: 
  • High jetness (deep black intensity) 
  • Excellent thermal stability 
  • High purity, minimal impurities that could affect polymer performance 
Careful pigment selection ensures a deep, sharp, and long-lasting black shade that does not fade over time. 

2. Premixing of raw materials

Carbon Black powder, PP carrier resin, and additives are blended together in precise ratios using industrial mixing systems.  The goal of premixing is to create a homogeneous mixture before melt extrusion.  Mascom Global employs high-speed mixers that: 
  • Increase blending uniformity 
  • Reduce processing time 
  • Enhance extrusion efficiency 

3. Melt extrusion & dispersion

The premixed materials are fed into a twin-screw extruder.  Inside the extruder, the following processes occur: 
  • PP resin is melted 
  • Carbon Black is dispersed uniformly into the polymer matrix 
  • Materials are continuously mixed under high shear and controlled pressure 
  • Air and impurities are removed through a vacuum degassing system 
Mascom Global invests in advanced extrusion technology that allows: 
  • Precise temperature control 
  • Ultra-fine pigment dispersion 
  • Improved mechanical strength of the final product 

4. Cooling & pelletizing

After extrusion, the molten polymer strand is cooled in water and then processed through an automatic pelletizing system to form uniform Black PP pellets.  Mascom Global’s pellet quality requirements include: 
  • Smooth, glossy surface with no air bubbles 
  • Consistent pellet size 
  • Low moisture content 
  • No clumping or contamination 

Black PP Masterbatch Production Process at Mascom Global 

5. Strict quality control (QC)

Quality control is a mandatory and rigorous step at Mascom Global.  Each batch is tested for: 
  • Blackness (jetness) and opacity 
  • Pigment dispersion quality 
  • Melt flow index (MFI) 
  • UV resistance 
  • Moisture and impurity levels 
Only qualified batches are approved for packaging and distribution. 6. Packaging & storage Black PP Masterbatch is packed in 25 kg moisture-proof bags and stored in clean, dry warehouse conditions that meet international export standards. 

Why customers choose Mascom Global’s Black PP Masterbatch? 

  • Highly consistent and stable quality 
  • Strong blackness – excellent dispersion – no streaking issues 
  • Suitable for a wide range of plastic applications 
  • Exceptional heat and UV resistance 
  • Competitive cost with high processing performance 
  • Dedicated technical support – customized formulations on request 
Mascom Global is committed to delivering the most effective and reliable black masterbatch solutions for plastics manufacturers worldwide.

item.title: White Masterbatch - Composition, Applications and Usages
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
1. What is White Masterbatch?

White Masterbatch is a type of color masterbatch made by mixing key components such as titanium dioxide pigment (TiO₂), carrier resin, and selected additives. It is designed to enhance whiteness, opacity, and surface gloss of plastic products — especially essential for applications requiring a pure white color, high coverage, and excellent appearance. Depending on the end-use requirement, the TiO₂ content in White Masterbatch typically ranges from 10% to 75%.

White Masterbatch at Mascom Global Factory

2. Main Components

Below are the key ingredients and their functions in White Masterbatch:
  • Titanium Dioxide (TiO₂): The main whitening pigment providing high opacity and brightness. With its high refractive index, TiO₂ efficiently scatters and reflects light, resulting in whiter, brighter, and more opaque plastic materials.
  • Carrier Resin: The base polymer that carries pigment and additives, ensuring uniform dispersion of TiO₂ into the final plastic. The carrier resin is selected based on compatibility with the end polymer (e.g., PE, PP, PS, ABS…).
  • Additives: May include UV stabilizers, antioxidants, dispersing agents, surface modifiers, and anti-yellowing agents to enhance performance, color stability, and outdoor durability.

3. Key Benefits and Functions

White Masterbatch provides multiple benefits for plastic production:
  • Improved Whiteness and Opacity: With high TiO₂ loading, it gives plastic products a pure white color and excellent hiding power, effectively masking base polymer color or impurities.
  • Enhanced Gloss and Aesthetic Value: Produces smooth, glossy surfaces that increase the visual appeal of plastic products such as packaging, household goods, and decorative parts.
  • UV Resistance and Weather Durability: TiO₂ not only creates whiteness but also absorbs and scatters UV light, improving outdoor performance and preventing discoloration or fading.
  • Better Dispersion and Production Stability: Using masterbatch instead of raw pigment reduces dust, improves color consistency, simplifies dosing, and enhances production efficiency.
  • Cost Optimization: A well-formulated masterbatch delivers desired properties with lower usage rates than dry pigments — reducing cost and improving process control.

4. Applications and Usage Instructions

Common Applications:

White Masterbatch is widely used across plastic industries in various applications, such as:
  • Film & Packaging: Blown film for shopping bags, garbage bags, agricultural film, food packaging, and industrial film.
  • Injection Molding: White-colored plastic items such as household goods, toys, containers, and decorative parts.
  • Blow Molding: Bottles, cans, and containers requiring high whiteness and surface brightness.
  • Extrusion: Sheets, pipes, and profiles made from PVC, PP, or PE needing excellent whiteness and smooth surfaces.
  • Other Industries: Construction materials (pipes, panels), automotive interior parts, electronics, and white appliance housings.

How to Use White Masterbatch?

When using White Masterbatch in production, consider the following steps:
  1. Select the right masterbatch based on your base polymer (PE, PP, PS, ABS, PVC…) to ensure good compatibility and dispersion.
  2. Determine the let-down ratio: Follow the manufacturer’s recommended dosage (typically 1–5%) to achieve the required whiteness and opacity.
  3. Mix and process properly: Ensure even blending of masterbatch and polymer during extrusion, blowing, or injection. Optimize machine settings (temperature, screw speed) to avoid streaks or poor dispersion.
  4. Quality control: Check whiteness level, gloss, coverage, and UV/yellowing resistance after production.
  5. Optimize cost-performance: Test different TiO₂ concentrations (e.g., 10–75%) to find the best balance between cost and desired appearance.

Why Choose Mascom Global White Masterbatch?

  • Formulated with TiO₂ content from 10% to 75%, suitable for diverse applications.
  • Compliant with EU RoHS, EN71-3, PAHs, PFOS/PFOA, and REACH-SVHC standards.
  • Produced by Mascom Global, a leading Vietnamese manufacturer specializing in Filler Masterbatch, Color Masterbatch, and Additive Masterbatch with modern production lines and international quality control systems.
Versatile applications: Designed for blown film, injection molding, and extrusion blow processes, exported to numerous countries worldwide.

item.title: Common Plastic Types and Applications – Choosing Plastic Types in Filler Masterbatch Production
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
1. Overview of Plastic Materials

Plastic is one of the most versatile materials used across modern industries, thanks to its lightweight, durability, flexibility, and ease of processing. Based on chemical properties, plastics are generally classified into two main categories: 
  • Thermoplastics (e.g., PP, PE, PVC, PS): can be melted and reshaped multiple times. 
  • Thermosets (e.g., PU, Epoxy): can only be molded once and retain their structure permanently. 
In filler masterbatch production, thermoplastics such as PP and PE (LDPE, LLDPE, and HDPE) are commonly used as base resins. Selecting the right polymer base is crucial for ensuring uniform CaCO₃ dispersion, mechanical strength, and production efficiency.  2. Common Types of Plastics and Their Applications

2.1. Polyethylene (PE) 

Characteristics: PE is the most widely used plastic in the industry and is available in two primary forms: 
  • LDPE (Low-Density Polyethylene): soft, flexible, and stretchable. 
  • HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene): strong, rigid, and chemical-resistant. 
Applications: 
  • LDPE: film packaging, plastic bags, stretch wrap, drip irrigation tubing. 
  • HDPE: bottles, containers, water pipes, household goods, and toys. 
Comment: PE is an ideal base resin for filler masterbatch due to its excellent compatibility with calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), enabling cost reduction while maintaining good flexibility and surface gloss. 

2.2. Polypropylene (PP) 

Characteristics: PP is lightweight, heat-resistant, durable, and easy to color.  Applications: Woven sacks, PP fibers, plastic containers, BOPP films, and injection-molded products.  Comment: PP is the most popular base polymer for filler masterbatch production. Adding filler enhances rigidity, improves heat resistance, and optimizes material costs — especially important in woven packaging, piping, and injection molding applications. 

2.3. Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) 

Characteristics: PVC offers good electrical insulation and flame resistance. When combined with plasticizers, it becomes flexible (soft PVC).  Applications: Pipes, cables, roofing sheets, films, and building materials.  Comment: Using filler masterbatch in PVC helps improve impact strength, lower production costs, and maintain surface smoothness. 

2.4. Polystyrene (PS) 

Characteristics: PS is transparent, rigid, but brittle. Two main types include: 
  • GPPS (General Purpose PS): clear and brittle. 
  • HIPS (High Impact PS): more flexible due to rubber content. 
Applications: Food packaging, disposable cups, plastic trays, and electronic casings. 3. Key Technical Parameters for Choosing Base Resin in Filler Masterbatch Selecting the right polymer base is vital to achieve optimal dispersion, stability, and quality in filler masterbatch production. Here are the most critical technical parameters to consider: 

3.1. Melt Flow Index (MFI / MI) 

Definition: Measures how easily the plastic flows under specific temperature and pressure. Meaning: A higher MFI → better flowability → improved CaCO₃ dispersion. Each application requires a specific MFI range for optimal processing. 

3.2. Crystallinity 

Affects the product’s stiffness, transparency, and shrinkage. Polymers with higher crystallinity (like PP and HDPE) produce stronger, more dimensionally stable filler compounds. 

3.3. Compatibility 

Indicates how well the polymer blends with CaCO₃ particles. Using coupling agents (e.g., stearic acid) improves compatibility and ensures even filler distribution. 

3.4. Moisture Content & Hygroscopicity 

Polymers with high moisture absorption (e.g., PE, PP, PA, PET) must be dried before processing to prevent voids, burn marks, or poor surface finish. 

3.5. Density (Specific Gravity) 

Directly affects blending ratios and product weight. Lightweight base resins (like PP and PE) help reduce raw material costs when mixed with filler. 

3.6. Melting Point 

Determines the optimal processing temperature in extruders and mixers. The base polymer’s melting point should align with CaCO₃ and additive stability to avoid material degradation. 4. Importance of Selecting the Right Base Resin A high-quality filler masterbatch depends not only on the purity of CaCO₃ but also on choosing the right base resin. Balancing MFI, crystallinity, and compatibility helps: 
  • Reduce energy consumption during production. 
  • Enhance filler dispersion and consistency. 
  • Maintain gloss, strength, and aesthetic appeal of the final product. 
Moreover, a suitable base polymer ensures compatibility with customers’ final resins, leading to stable and flexible product performance across multiple applications. 5. Conclusion Each plastic type has unique properties suited for specific industrial applications. In filler masterbatch manufacturing, understanding the polymer’s structure and technical parameters is the key to achieving the best results in both quality and cost efficiency.  An optimized filler masterbatch not only reduces production costs but also improves product durability, gloss, printability, and processing performance — helping Vietnamese manufacturers enhance their global competitiveness in the plastics industry.

item.title: Plastic vs Rubber: Understanding the Differences
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In the field of polymer materials, plastics and rubber are the two most common materials, present in almost every sector from industrial production, consumer goods, to high-tech applications. However, although both belong to the polymer group, plastics and rubber have entirely different properties, leading to significant differences in applications and value.  This article will help you gain a deeper understanding of the nature, characteristics, and technical factors that distinguish these two important materials.

1. Definition and Nature

Plastic is a type of polymer that can be shaped under the influence of heat and pressure, and retains a fixed form once cooled. Depending on the structure and composition, plastics are divided into two main groups: 
  • Thermoplastics: Can be melted and reshaped multiple times (e.g., PE, PP, PVC, ABS…). 
  • Thermosets: Once set, they cannot be remelted (e.g., epoxy, phenolic…). 
Rubber is also a polymer, but is characterized by high elasticity. It can be stretched, compressed, or deformed under force, and then return to its original shape when the force is removed. To achieve stable properties, rubber must undergo vulcanization — crosslinking polymer chains using sulfur or chemical agents, enhancing durability and environmental resistance.

2. Fundamental Differences Between Plastics and Rubber

Plastic 

  • Plastic is a highly moldable material, soft and flexible when heated, and solidifies when cooled. 
  • Its structure consists of long polymer chains, creating many types of plastics with distinct properties. 
  • Classification: Thermoplastics: can be melted and reshaped multiple times. Thermosets: can only be shaped once and cannot be remelted. 
  • Advantages: high rigidity, lightweight, easy to process. 
  • Applications: packaging, electronic components, consumer devices, and engineering materials. 
  • In manufacturing, plastics are often supplemented with Filler Masterbatch (CaCO₃ granules) to increase hardness, stabilize dimensions, and reduce cost; excessive use may make the material brittle and reduce impact resistance. 
  • Environmental impact: lightweight, reducing transportation energy; however, most plastics are petroleum-based, non-biodegradable. 
  • Development trends: recycled plastics, bioplastics, and chemical recycling technologies are being promoted to minimize environmental impact and move toward a circular economy. 

Rubber 

  • Rubber is distinguished by high elasticity, capable of stretching and returning to its original shape after force is removed. 
  • This property comes from flexible polymer chains stabilized through vulcanization using sulfur or chemical agents. 
  • Advantages: durable, wear-resistant, does not soften at high temperatures. 
  • Types: Natural rubber (NR): derived from Hevea brasiliensis latex. Synthetic rubber: SBR, NBR, EPDM, silicone, each with specific properties (NBR oil-resistant, EPDM ozone-resistant, silicone heat and chemical-resistant). 
  • Applications: tires, gaskets, seals, cushions, flexible hoses, and insulating materials. 
  • Environmental impact: natural rubber is more biodegradable, but large-scale cultivation requires sustainable management. Synthetic rubber relies on petroleum, causing emissions similar to plastics. 
  • Recycling: challenging due to vulcanized cross-linked networks; devulcanization technologies and reuse of crumb rubber in asphalt, playgrounds, and construction materials help reduce waste and extend product life. 

3. Industrial Applications

In practical production, plastics are favored for their low cost, light weight, and ease of molding. Typical products include packaging, bottles, electronic components, automotive parts, construction materials, and consumer goods. Plastics can also be blended with Filler Masterbatch (CaCO₃) or Additive Masterbatch to improve performance, save costs, and increase mechanical strength.  Rubber, on the other hand, is chosen for applications requiring elasticity, compressive strength, vibration resistance, and impact resistance. It is indispensable in the automotive, aerospace, mechanical, electronics, and medical industries. Common types like NR (natural rubber), NBR (nitrile rubber), EPDM, or silicone rubber are used depending on the environment and technical requirements. 

4. Advantages and Disadvantages of Each Material

Plastics are lightweight, inexpensive, suitable for mass production, and can generate thousands of variations through polymer blending technology. However, plastics are often less elastic and brittle at low temperatures.  Rubber excels in elasticity, impact resistance, and sealing capability, but vulcanization is more complex, production costs are higher, and recycling options are limited. 

5. Trends in Combining Plastics and Rubber

Today, with advancements in material science, manufacturers are moving toward blending plastics and rubber to create Thermoplastic Elastomers (TPE), which combine the elasticity of rubber with the processability and recyclability of plastics. This is a prominent trend in modern polymer industries, optimizing costs while supporting environmental protection.

6. Conclusion

Although both are polymers, plastics and rubber serve different needs. Plastics are suitable for products requiring rigidity, precision, and ease of processing, while rubber is ideal for products needing elasticity, pressure resistance, and sealing performance.  Understanding the differences between these materials helps businesses select the right raw materials, optimize production efficiency, reduce costs, and improve final product quality. Additionally, awareness of the environmental implications of each material can guide sustainable product development and responsible material choices.  At Mascom Global, we provide high-quality plastic material solutions, including Colored plastics, Filler Masterbatch, Technical plastic compounds, and Additive masterbatches. With advanced technology and an experienced engineering team, we accompany customers from material selection to developing optimal formulas, ensuring products meet the highest technical standards while remaining environmentally friendly.  Explore Mascom Global’s solutions to upgrade your products, optimize production processes, and move toward a sustainable future in the plastics and rubber industry.
