item.title: Additive Masterbatch - Common Issues & Solutions
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
MASCOM GLOBAL - Common Issues in Additive Masterbatch and Effective Troubleshooting Methods 

Additive masterbatch plays a vital role in modern polymer processing, enhancing plastic performance by providing properties such as UV resistance, flame retardancy, anti-static behavior, and thermal stability. However, during production and application, various defects can occur that affect both product quality and processing efficiency. Understanding these common issues and how to address them is crucial for ensuring consistent performance in plastic manufacturing.

1. Poor Dispersion of Additives

Problem: One of the most frequent issues with additive masterbatch is poor dispersion of active ingredients within the polymer matrix. This often results in visible streaks, color spots, or inconsistent surface appearance. Poor dispersion can also reduce the effectiveness of functional additives like UV stabilizers or antioxidants. Causes:
  • Incompatible carrier resin with the base polymer.
  • Insufficient mixing time or inadequate screw design in extrusion.
  • High additive loading beyond the carrier’s saturation limit.
Solutions:
  • Choose a carrier resin that matches the polarity and melt flow index (MFI) of the target polymer.
  • Optimize processing parameters such as temperature profile and screw speed to enhance shear mixing.
  • Use advanced dispersing agents or coupling agents to improve compatibility between the additive and polymer.
  • For critical applications, employ twin-screw extruders with appropriate mixing elements for uniform distribution.

2. Moisture Absorption and Volatility

Problem: Moisture absorption in additive masterbatch can lead to surface defects such as bubbles, voids, or haze in the final product. In hygroscopic materials, moisture can also degrade sensitive additives like antioxidants or hinder proper polymer flow. Causes:
  • Improper drying or storage conditions.
  • Use of hygroscopic carriers like nylon or PET without proper moisture control.
  • Inadequate packaging that allows ambient humidity to penetrate.
Solutions:
  • Pre-dry both base resin and masterbatch before processing, especially for engineering plastics.
  • Use moisture-barrier packaging and store masterbatch in controlled environments.
  • Introduce desiccant additives or employ vacuum venting during extrusion for moisture-sensitive formulations.

3. Poor Compatibility Between Additive and Base Polymer

Problem: If the additive masterbatch is not fully compatible with the host polymer, phase separation or uneven additive distribution may occur. This can manifest as surface blooming, poor mechanical strength, or inconsistent performance of the final product. Causes:
  • Carrier resin mismatch with the base polymer.
  • Chemical incompatibility between additive molecules and polymer chains.
  • Improper additive selection or incorrect dosage levels.
Solutions:
  • Match carrier resin as closely as possible to the target polymer type.
  • Modify additive chemistry (e.g., using compatibilizers or coupling agents) to improve interaction.
  • Conduct pilot testing to optimize the masterbatch concentration for the specific end-use polymer.

4. Degradation During Processing

Problem: Thermal or mechanical degradation of additives during extrusion or molding can cause discoloration, odor formation, or reduced additive functionality. Causes:
  • Excessive processing temperature or residence time.
  • Inadequate temperature control in the extruder zones.
  • Shear overheating due to high screw speed.
Solutions:
  • Optimize processing conditions — lower barrel temperatures or adjust screw configuration to reduce shear stress.
  • Select heat-stabilized additive systems that can withstand processing conditions.
  • Add processing stabilizers such as antioxidants or phosphites to protect the polymer-additive system.

5. Additive Migration and Surface Blooming

Problem: Additive migration occurs when active components migrate to the surface of the final product, resulting in a white haze or oily film known as blooming. This phenomenon can compromise surface appearance, printability, or adhesion. Causes:
  • Over-concentration of additives.
  • Low molecular weight or poor compatibility of additives with polymer matrix.
  • Inadequate curing or cooling conditions.
Solutions:
  • Optimize additive dosage to avoid oversaturation.
  • Choose high-molecular-weight or polymer-bound additives to reduce mobility.
  • Improve cooling cycles or post-treatment processes to lock additives within the polymer structure.

6. Inconsistent Additive Performance

Problem: Inconsistent additive activity — such as fluctuating UV protection, anti-blocking effect, or slip performance — can occur due to uneven distribution or additive deactivation. Causes:
  • Variation in masterbatch production parameters.
  • Poor additive quality or contamination.
  • Aging of the masterbatch during storage.
Solutions:
  • Implement strict quality control during compounding (e.g., melt flow rate, dispersion index, and active content testing).
  • Ensure raw material consistency and maintain proper inventory rotation (FIFO).
  • Protect masterbatch from UV exposure and high temperatures during storage.

Conclusion

Additive Masterbatch formulation and processing require a delicate balance between chemistry, compatibility, and processing conditions. By identifying and addressing issues such as poor dispersion, moisture absorption, or additive migration early, manufacturers can maintain stable production and ensure high-quality end products. Continuous monitoring, advanced formulation design, and close cooperation between polymer engineers and additive suppliers are key to achieving consistent, high-performance masterbatch solutions.

item.title: Additive Masterbatch - Enhancing Nylon Bag Production Efficiency
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In today’s highly competitive plastics industry, manufacturers of nylon bags (PE, HDPE, LDPE, etc.) face not only intense cost pressures, but also growing demands for better product quality, durability, and eco-friendliness. To stay ahead in this challenging environment, factories must constantly optimize their production processes, reduce waste, and deliver consistent performance. One of the most effective solutions to achieve these goals is the use of Additive Masterbatch — a powerful yet cost-efficient way to enhance the functionality and processability of polymer products. 

1. What is Additive Masterbatch?

Additive Masterbatch is a concentrated mixture of functional additives uniformly dispersed in a carrier resin such as PE, PP, or EVA. When blended with virgin or recycled resin at a specific ratio, it enhances product performance without altering the polymer’s fundamental structure or mechanical strength.  Depending on production requirements, the most common types of Additive Masterbatch used in nylon bag manufacturing include:  Slip Agent – reduces surface friction and facilitates smooth film movement during winding and bag-making.  Anti-block Agent – prevents film layers from sticking to each other, ensuring easy separation and handling.  Anti-static Agent – reduces electrostatic charge that attracts dust or causes film sticking.  UV Stabilizer – protects the film from ultraviolet degradation during outdoor storage or use.  Antioxidant – prevents oxidation and thermal degradation during processing.  Processing Aid – enhances melt flow, film clarity, and extrusion stability.  Each additive plays a distinct but complementary role. When formulated correctly, they help streamline production, minimize downtime, and extend equipment lifespan — leading to both technical and financial advantages. 

2. Benefits of Using Additive Masterbatch in Nylon Bag Production

Improved processing and higher productivity

Additives such as Processing Aid or Slip Agent create a smoother interface between the polymer melt and the machinery surface. This reduces melt friction and die pressure, preventing problems like die build-up, sharkskin defects, or gel formation. Manufacturers have reported up to 10–20% higher extrusion speed, along with noticeable reductions in energy consumption and maintenance frequency — translating into lower overall production costs.

Enhanced surface quality

Without proper additives, nylon bags often become sticky, scratched, or difficult to separate. By adding Anti-block and Slip Agents, the surface smoothness and slip performance are significantly improved, resulting in easier handling, cutting, and printing. For premium packaging such as shopping bags, garment bags, or fashion pouches, these additives provide a glossy, soft-touch, and high-clarity finish, elevating product aesthetics and brand perception.

Greater durability and longer shelf life

Nylon bags used for outdoor or export applications are exposed to UV radiation and oxygen, which can cause yellowing, brittleness, or cracking. Incorporating UV Stabilizers and Antioxidants prevents polymer degradation, extending the bag’s functional lifespan by two to three times compared with untreated materials. This durability not only improves user satisfaction but also helps brands meet environmental standards by reducing waste from premature product failure.

Lower raw material costs

With the help of Additive Masterbatch, manufacturers can safely increase the proportion of recycled resin while still maintaining mechanical strength, flexibility, and transparency. This is a crucial advantage amid fluctuating virgin resin prices. By using high-quality masterbatch, factories can cut raw material costs by up to 15% without compromising on performance or appearance.

Environmental and sustainability advantages

Modern additive technologies enable thinner film production without sacrificing strength — reducing plastic consumption per unit. In addition, improved durability means fewer defective or discarded bags, contributing to a more sustainable and circular production model. 

3. Real-World Applications in Nylon Bag Production

Across Asia and Europe, many leading film manufacturers have adopted Additive Masterbatch to: 
  • Increase film-blowing and bag-making speed without expensive equipment upgrades 
  • Reduce defect rates (sticking, pinholes, wrinkles) by 5 – 10% 
  • Improve film flatness and printability for supermarket, garbage, and food packaging bags 
  • Enhance aesthetic quality, clarity, and mechanical strength for export-grade products 
  • Achieve better winding stability and film roll consistency during high-speed operations 
These improvements directly translate to fewer rejects, faster cycles, and higher profitability. 

4. Choosing High-Quality Additive Masterbatch – The Key Factor

The performance of Additive Masterbatch depends largely on its formulation accuracy, additive purity, and dispersion quality. Therefore, nylon bag manufacturers should choose reliable suppliers with technical expertise, customization capability, and consistent quality control.  In Vietnam, companies such as Mascom Global have developed advanced Additive Masterbatch solutions tailored for PE, HDPE, and LDPE bag production. Their formulations help reduce film friction, improve clarity, stabilize color, and optimize processing efficiency — supporting customers in achieving both cost and quality targets.

5. Conclusion

The integration of Additive Masterbatch in nylon bag production represents a smart, sustainable, and high-value approach to modern manufacturing. It not only enhances processing efficiency and product performance but also enables manufacturers to lower costs, improve quality consistency, and extend both product and machinery lifespan.  In an era where productivity, innovation, and sustainability define success, companies that leverage advanced additive technologies like Additive Masterbatch gain a long-term competitive advantage — achieving high-quality production, stronger brand value, and sustainable profitability in the global mark.

item.title: Common Defects of Filler Masterbatch in Film Blowing - Applications and Solutions
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In the plastic packaging industry, Filler Masterbatch plays an essential role in reducing production costs while improving product strength, stiffness, and opacity. However, during the film blowing process, improper formulation or handling of filler can lead to several processing and quality issues that directly affect the appearance and mechanical performance of the final film.  Below are the most common problems and professional solutions, summarized from the practical experience of Mascom Global JSC — a leading manufacturer of Filler, Color, and Additive Masterbatch in Vietnam. 

1. White Spots and Rough Film Surface

Causes: 
  • Poor dispersion of the filler due to low-quality production or incompatible processing equipment. 
  • Filler resin base not matching the main polymer used in the final film. 
  • Product deterioration caused by long storage time or improper handling conditions. 
Solutions: To eliminate this issue, manufacturers should choose a filler grade with a high level of dispersion and better resin compatibility. If the film blowing machine is not suitable, the material can be used for alternative applications such as extrusion or injection molding, and a new filler grade optimized for film blowing should be recommended. Adjusting the extruder temperature profile may also help improve dispersion and surface smoothness. In cases where the filler has been stored for a long time, it is advisable to reduce the filler ratio or use it for less demanding products to avoid surface roughness.

2. “Fish Eyes” or Bubbles on the Film Surface

Causes: 
  • Excessive moisture in filler or recycled resin. 
Solutions: This problem can be solved by pre-drying the filler before feeding it into the extruder or by adding a moisture-absorbing additive to the compound. If the issue persists or the customer targets high-end applications, Mascom recommends using a premium filler grade with a very low moisture level and improved dispersion quality. Proper control of storage humidity and raw material handling is also crucial to prevent this recurring issue.

3. Poor Film Gloss

Causes: 
  • Inappropriate calcium carbonate particle size or surface coating. 
  • Non-optimized formulation leading to poor surface finish. 
Solutions: To enhance film gloss, manufacturers should select filler grades with smaller CaCO₃ particle sizes and optimized coating treatment. Alternatively, adding a small percentage of LDPE can help improve surface smoothness and light reflection. Mascom’s technical team can also assist in adjusting the compound formula to achieve the desired gloss level without compromising mechanical strength.

4. Unstable Bubble or Film Vibration During Blowing

Causes: 
  • The melt flow index (MFI) of the filler masterbatch does not match the resin matrix. 
  • Inconsistent or unstable air flow during the blowing process. 
Solutions: An unstable bubble can be corrected by adjusting the extrusion temperature and air pressure settings to ensure steady melt viscosity. In the long term, customers should consider using a filler grade with a compatible MFI, which ensures smooth extrusion and uniform bubble formation. Regular maintenance and calibration of the film blowing equipment are also recommended for optimal stability.

5. Low Film Strength or Poor Elongation

Causes: 
  • Incompatible filler resin or excessive filler loading. 
  • Customer’s formulation not optimized for performance. 
  • Improper air flow or cooling speed in the film blowing process. 
Solutions: Mascom suggests modifying the filler formula to ensure better bonding between the filler and the polymer matrix. Customers should optimize the compound ratio between filler and virgin resin to maintain the right balance between stiffness and flexibility. Additionally, adjusting the film blowing parameters (such as blow-up ratio, air pressure, and cooling temperature) can significantly enhance tensile strength and elongation.

6. Film Breakage During Production

Causes: 
  • Poor filler dispersion or contamination in the mixture. 
  • Inappropriate particle size of CaCO₃. 
  • Blocked filter screens reducing material flow. 
Solutions: To prevent film breakage, manufacturers should use filler with high dispersion quality and clean raw materials free from impurities. Regular inspection and replacement of filter meshes are necessary to maintain smooth extrusion. Mascom also recommends optimizing the filler particle size to ensure consistent melt flow and eliminate stress points that lead to film tearing.

7. Film Too White or Too Dark

Causes: 
  • Excessive whiteness caused by high TiO₂ content or ultra-white calcium carbonate. 
  • Low-quality filler resulting in a dull or grayish tone. 
  • Incompatible resin base leading to poor color consistency. 
Solutions: To correct film color imbalance, select a filler grade with appropriate whiteness and controlled TiO₂ content. For overly white films, switching to a filler with lower brightness or reduced TiO₂ level can restore the desired shade. For darker or dull films, adding OB-1 or high-quality TiO₂ pigment is recommended to improve brightness and transparency. In all cases, matching the filler resin with the main polymer is essential for stable optical performance. 

Why Choose Mascom Global JSC as Your Filler Masterbatch Partner? 

Mascom Global JSC not only delivers consistent quality and competitive pricing, but also provides comprehensive technical support throughout the production process. With a skilled R&D team, advanced quality control system (DSC, TGA, MFI, Spectrophotometer), and flexible custom production, Mascom ensures the most efficient and reliable filler solutions for every film blowing application.

item.title: Common Defects in White Masterbatch and How to Resolve
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
White Masterbatch is one of the most essential materials in the plastics industry. It provides brightness, opacity, and enhanced mechanical properties for final products, ensuring both aesthetic and functional performance. From film blowing and injection molding to extrusion and thermoforming, the quality of white masterbatch has a direct impact on product consistency and efficiency.  However, when the masterbatch formulation, pigment dispersion, or processing parameters are not optimized, several defects may occur — affecting surface finish, whiteness, and long-term stability. Understanding these problems and their causes allows manufacturers to implement effective corrective actions, maintaining both product quality and production stability.  Below is an in-depth analysis of the most common defects in White Masterbatch and practical ways to resolve them. 

1. Uneven Whiteness or Streaking

This defect frequently appears in film blowing, extrusion, and injection molding applications. It leads to visible color inconsistency, streaks, or cloudy surfaces.  Main causes include: 
  • Poor dispersion of TiO₂ pigments within the polymer matrix 
  • Agglomeration of TiO₂ particles 
  • Inadequate melt temperature 
  • Improper screw speed or back pressure 
Recommended solutions: 
  • Select high-dispersion White Masterbatch produced with twin-screw compounding technology 
  • Increase melt temperature to improve pigment distribution 
  • Adjust screw speed and back pressure for better mixing 
  • Use Rutile TiO₂, which offers stronger opacity and more stable whiteness than Anatase 

2. Low Whiteness or Dull, Greyish Appearance

When the final product lacks brightness or appears slightly yellowish, it usually indicates issues related to pigment loading or raw material quality.  Causes: 
  • Insufficient TiO₂ content 
  • Use of Anatase TiO₂ that tends to discolor under heat or UV 
  • Poor-quality or oxidized base resin 
Solutions: 
  • Choose a masterbatch containing 50–75% TiO₂, depending on the application 
  • Prefer organic-coated Rutile TiO₂ for better heat and UV resistance 
  • Store materials in a dry, cool environment to prevent degradation 
  • For high-end applications, verify Lab color values* to ensure consistent whiteness 

3. Spots, Undispersed Particles, or Fish Eyes

These small defects are highly visible in thin films or glossy molded parts, negatively affecting product aesthetics.  Causes: 
  • Pigment agglomeration due to poor premixing 
  • Low melt temperature resulting in incomplete dispersion 
  • Moisture or contamination in the raw materials 
Solutions: 
  • Use twin-screw extruded masterbatch for uniform pigment distribution 
  • Increase melt temperature or adjust screw speed to allow more mixing time 
  • Ensure proper drying of raw materials before processing 

4. Yellowing or Discoloration Over Time

This defect is often observed in products exposed to sunlight, heat, or harsh environments.  Causes: 
  • Use of Anatase TiO₂, which is UV-sensitive 
  • Overheating during processing 
  • Incompatibility among additives or resins 
Solutions: 
  • Select Rutile TiO₂ with organic coating for superior UV resistance 
  • Optimize machine temperature profiles to prevent polymer degradation 
  • Ensure formulation compatibility among all additives and base resins 

5. Poor Opacity or Insufficient Coverage

A translucent or uneven white appearance indicates a lack of opacity, which is critical for packaging and film products.  Causes: 
  • Low masterbatch dosage 
  • Inadequate TiO₂ concentration 
  • Oversized pigment particles reducing light scattering efficiency 
Solutions: 
  • Increase masterbatch dosage to 2 – 8% depending on thickness and resin type 
  • Use TiO₂ with particle size around 0.2 – 0.3 µm for optimal opacity 
  • Check whiteness index and coverage before mass production 

6. Poor Surface Gloss or Rough Texture

Surface smoothness and gloss are key for cosmetic, consumer, and household products.  Causes: 
  • Poor pigment dispersion 
  • Excessive masterbatch dosage 
  • Incorrect extrusion temperature or screw configuration 
Solutions: 
  • Reduce masterbatch ratio or switch to a high-dispersion grade 
  • Adjust processing parameters to optimize flow and surface finish 
  • Use formulations containing surface-enhancing additives to improve gloss

Recommendations for Selecting High-Quality White Masterbatch 

To minimize the above issues and maintain consistent product quality, manufacturers should: 
  • Use high TiO₂ concentration (preferably Rutile grade) 
  • Ensure excellent pigment dispersion through twin-screw compounding 
  • Verify whiteness index, opacity, and consistency across batches 
  • Work with suppliers offering technical support and strict quality control

item.title: Can Additive Masterbatch Improve Production Efficiency and Energy Consumption?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
As the global plastics industry faces growing pressure from rising energy costs and sustainability demands, Additive Masterbatch is emerging as a key solution to optimize processes, save energy, and enhance product performance. In particular, Mascom Global’s Additive Masterbatch line has gained recognition from manufacturers worldwide for its ability to improve production efficiency and reduce operational costs significantly.

1. What is Additive Masterbatch?

Additive Masterbatch is a concentrated blend of base resin (typically PE or PP) and functional additives. Manufacturers only need to mix a small amount (1 – 5%) with the main polymer to achieve the desired effects. Mascom Global’s Additive Masterbatch Solutions are designed for industrial optimization:
  • Antioxidant – Prevents thermal degradation and polymer aging during processing.
  • UV Stabilizer – Protects products from UV radiation, extending outdoor lifespan.
  • Slip & Antiblock – Improves surface smoothness and reduces friction.
  • Processing Aid – Enhances polymer flow and reduces melt fracture.
  • Antistatic, Antibacterial, Flame Retardant, etc. – Offers protection and stability for specialized applications.
All Mascom Global additives use virgin PP or PE carrier resin, ensuring excellent dispersion, compatibility, and real-world energy savings. Many production facilities have reported up to 12% higher output and 8% lower energy consumption after switching to Mascom Global Additive Masterbatch.

2. How Additive Masterbatch Helps Save Energy

Additive Masterbatch contributes to energy savings through three main mechanisms: (1) Reducing Friction and Improving Polymer Flow  Additives such as Processing Aid or Slip Masterbatch help polymer melt move more smoothly through the extruder and die, minimizing sticking to metal surfaces. ➡ Results:
  • Lower extrusion pressure → reduced motor power usage
  • Less polymer degradation → fewer shutdowns and maintenance needs
(2) Enhancing Thermal Efficiency and Shortening Cycle Time  Certain Antioxidants and Processing aid enable processing at lower temperatures while maintaining desired melt flow. ➡ Results:
  • Reduced heating energy
  • Shorter molding/blowing cycles → higher productivity on the same machine
(3) Minimizing Waste and Machine Cleaning Time  Well-dispersed additives stabilize polymer flow, reducing common defects like burning, discoloration, or fiber breakage. ➡ Results:
  • Less raw material waste
  • Less downtime for cleaning or maintenance

3. Specific Benefits in Common Plastic Processes

  • Film Blowing
  • Additives improve film gloss, smoothness, and heat resistance. Reduced friction allows faster film output (10 – 12% speed increase) while maintaining thickness uniformity.
  • Raffia / Woven Sack Production Processing Aid helps maintain yarn stability and reduce breakage, resulting in lower energy use during stretching and weaving.
  • Injection Molding Additives enhance mold filling and cooling efficiency, cutting cycle time by 5 – 8% and lowering energy consumption for both injection and cooling systems.

4. Common Energy-Saving Additives

Additive Type Main Function Energy Efficiency Benefit
Processing Aid Reduces friction, improves polymer flow Lowers extrusion pressure and motor power consumption
Antioxidant Stabilizes polymer during heating Allows lower processing temperatures
Slip / Antiblock Improves film slip and separation Reduces mechanical friction, increases production speed
According to internal studies at major film and raffia manufacturers, the use of Processing Aid Masterbatch can cut energy consumption by 5 – 10% while boosting output by 8 – 12% without extra cleaning or maintenance.

5. Impact on Sustainability and Environmental Goals

Beyond direct energy savings, Additive Masterbatch helps manufacturers move toward greener production:
  • Lower power usage → Reduced CO₂ emissions
  • Longer product lifespan (via UV Stabilizer & Antioxidant) → Less plastic waste
  • Higher productivity → Less energy per unit output
These benefits align with the global trend of sustainable manufacturing, where energy efficiency and carbon reduction are now key performance indicators in the international supply chain. Mascom Global continues to innovate eco-friendly Additive Masterbatch solutions, helping customers enhance performance, reduce costs, and strengthen competitiveness worldwide.

6. Conclusion

Additive Masterbatch is more than just a plastic additive — it’s a strategic tool for manufacturers aiming for smarter, more efficient, and sustainable production. With advanced formulation technology and proven performance, Mascom Global’s Additive Masterbatch empowers manufacturers to achieve higher efficiency, better quality, and lower energy costs — a true step forward toward sustainable industrial growth.

item.title: The Appropriate Filler Masterbatch Loading Rate for Different Plastic Applications
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In the plastics industry, selecting the appropriate Filler Masterbatch ratio (CaCO₃ Filler) is a key factor that determines production efficiency, product quality, and material cost. Each plastic application — from packaging films and thermoforming sheets to pipes and non-woven fabrics — has specific mechanical and surface requirements. Therefore, the filler ratio must be adjusted accordingly to achieve optimal performance.

1️⃣ Filler Masterbatch – Balancing Cost and Performance

Filler Masterbatch is a cost-effective additive widely used in the plastics industry. It consists of ultra-fine calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) dispersed in polymer carriers such as PP, PE, PS, or PVC. A small amount of dispersing or coupling agents is added to improve compatibility and flow during processing. When blended with virgin resin, Filler Masterbatch provides several notable benefits:
  • 💰 Significant cost reduction: CaCO₃ filler replaces part of the more expensive polymer resin, lowering raw material costs without sacrificing essential properties.
  • ⚙️ Enhanced stiffness and dimensional stability: Filler improves rigidity, reduces deformation, and helps products maintain their shape during forming and cooling.
  • ⚡ Reduced shrinkage and static charge: This leads to smoother printing, improved handling, and better mechanical stability during production.
  • 🔥 Improved thermal stability and heat dissipation: CaCO₃ helps distribute heat more evenly, reducing the chances of warping and ensuring consistent product quality.
  • 🧪 Better processability: Filler can improve melt strength and extrusion smoothness in applications like blown film or sheet extrusion.
However, choosing the correct loading rate is critical. Using too little filler fails to optimize cost, while excessive usage may cause brittleness, reduced tensile strength, or compromised appearance.

2️⃣ Recommended Filler Masterbatch Ratios by Application

Below is a practical guideline for filler usage across major plastic applications. Actual ratios may vary depending on resin quality, product requirements, and machine conditions.
No. Plastic Applications Base Resin Filler Masterbatch Ratio Key Benefits
1 Blown Film (garbage bags, carry bags, shopping bags, agricultural films, industrial packaging bags, liners, etc.) LDPE / LLDPE / HDPE 10 – 50% Maintain flexibility, improve film drawability.
2 Pipe Extrusion PP / PE / PVC 10 – 40% Increase stiffness, stabilize pipe diameter.
3 Tarpaulin HDPE 10 – 30% Improve stiffness and dimensional stability while retaining adequate flexibility.
4 Blow Molding (bottles, cans, drums) HDPE / PP 10 – 30% Optimize container rigidity, reduce resin cost.
5 Injection Molding PP / PS / HIPS 10 – 30% Stabilize dimensions, reduce shrinkage.
6 Thermoforming PP / PS / PET 15 – 40% Increase stiffness, reduce deformation during forming.
7 PP Woven Sack / Raffia PP 10 – 35% Reduce yarn cost, increase stiffness and fabric strength.
8 Non-Woven Fabric PP 10 – 35% Improve surface smoothness, reduce static.
9 PVC Compound PVC 20 – 50% Enhance compressive strength and surface hardness.
Choosing the correct filler ratio depends on several important factors:

• Polymer Type

PP and PE generally allow higher filler loading than PET or PS due to better bonding between CaCO₃ and polyolefins.

• Mechanical and Visual Requirements

Products requiring transparency, high impact resistance, or strong tensile strength typically require lower filler ratios.

• CaCO₃ Particle Size

Ultra-fine particles (1 – 2 μm) disperse more effectively, enabling higher filler levels while maintaining good surface quality and mechanical strength.

• Machine Technology

Machines with stable temperature zones, proper screw design, and precise die control can handle higher filler content with better dispersion.

• End-use Functionality

Applications like food packaging or medical films may require stricter mechanical or safety standards, affecting allowable filler levels.

4️⃣ Mascom Global Solutions

With extensive export experience to over 30 markets, Mascom Global offers specialized filler masterbatches engineered for maximum performance:
  • 🟡 PP Filler Masterbatch – optimized for woven sacks, thermoforming, and injection molding.
  • 🟢 PE Filler Masterbatch – suitable for blown film, blow molding, and extrusion.
  • 🔵 PVC Filler Masterbatch – ideal for pipes, profiles, and general-purpose compounds.
All Mascom products are manufactured with:
  • Particle size D97 < 5 μm
  • Whiteness index > 98%
  • Excellent dispersion
  • High thermal stability
  • Controlled moisture and CO₂ content
This ensures customers can achieve high filler levels without compromising quality.

5️⃣ Practical Operation & Testing Considerations

To determine the optimal filler loading for your application, consider the following:
  • Start with small steps: Begin with 10 – 15% loading, then gradually increase while monitoring flexibility, tensile strength, and overall performance.
  • Control processing temperature: Excessive heat can cause yellowing or reduce gloss. Optimal temperature improves dispersion and surface quality.
  • Ensure proper drying: Moisture in filler can cause bubbles, fish-eyes, or voids in the final product. Pre-drying improves consistency.
  • Evaluate appearance and functionality: Look for uniform color, smooth surface, printability, and lack of haze or streaks.
  • Match carrier resin with your base polymer: Using PP-based filler for PP and PE-based filler for PE ensures compatibility and superior bonding.

🌍 Conclusion

Choosing the appropriate Filler Masterbatch ratio is essential for balancing cost savings with product performance. When used correctly, filler masterbatch can significantly decrease production expenses while improving dimensional stability, processing efficiency, and surface properties. At Mascom Global, we deliver not just high-quality filler masterbatch but also comprehensive technical support to help customers optimize every application — from blown film and injection molding to raffia, thermoforming, and PVC extrusion. 🌟 Mascom Global – Real Value Commitment Contact us for detailed technical advice tailored to your production needs.

item.title: Bio Filler Masterbatch – Driving Sustainable and Efficient Plastic Manufacturing
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
The global plastics industry is evolving rapidly, driven by increasing demand for sustainable production, cost efficiency, and high-quality materials. Traditional plastic products rely heavily on virgin polymers, which not only increase production costs but also contribute significantly to environmental impact, including carbon emissions and plastic waste. In response to these challenges, Bio Filler Masterbatch has emerged as a key innovation, offering manufacturers a practical and sustainable solution to produce high-performance plastics while reducing costs and environmental footprint.

1. What is Bio Filler Masterbatch?

Bio Filler Masterbatch is a pre-dispersed blend of a polymer carrier and bio-based or eco-friendly fillers. Common examples include: 
  • Calcium carbonate from renewable sources
  • Cellulose or plant-derived powders
  • Starch or other biodegradable fillers
Unlike conventional fillers, bio fillers are engineered to replace a portion of virgin polymer without compromising the mechanical, thermal, or aesthetic properties of the final product. The masterbatch format ensures that fillers are evenly distributed within the polymer matrix, which simplifies processing and minimizes common production issues such as clumping, uneven dispersion, or surface imperfections.  This versatility makes Bio Filler Masterbatch suitable for multiple plastic processing methods, including extrusion, injection molding, film blowing, and compounding. By integrating bio fillers at the masterbatch stage, manufacturers can achieve consistent quality and predictable performance in the final products. 

2. Key Advantages of Bio Filler Masterbatch

2.1 Cost Savings 

Bio Filler Masterbatch allows manufacturers to reduce raw material costs significantly. By substituting part of the virgin polymer with bio-based fillers, companies can achieve 20 – 30% savings on material costs, depending on the formulation. The pre-dispersed nature of masterbatch also ensures precise dosing and volumetric feeding, reducing waste and optimizing production efficiency. These benefits are especially valuable in high-volume production lines where raw material costs are a major component of overall expenses. 

2.2 Enhanced Product Quality 

Uniform filler dispersion is one of the key advantages of Bio Filler Masterbatch, leading to: 
  • Improved mechanical strength and rigidity
  • Smoother surfaces and better finish
  • Dimensional stability and reduced warpage
  • Consistent color and opacity
Applications such as woven and non-woven fabrics, films, sheets, and injection-molded components benefit directly, with fewer defects such as fiber breakage, film tearing, or surface irregularities. Manufacturers can deliver products that meet customer expectations and industrial quality standards consistently. 

2.3 Sustainable Manufacturing 

Sustainability has become a major priority for manufacturers and consumers alike. Using bio-based fillers reduces dependency on virgin plastics and helps lower environmental impact. Many bio fillers are renewable, biodegradable, or recyclable, supporting the principles of a circular economy. Incorporating Bio Filler Masterbatch into production enables companies to meet regulatory requirements, achieve sustainability certifications, and appeal to environmentally conscious markets. 

2.4 Improved Processing Efficiency 

Bio Filler Masterbatch enhances production efficiency by providing stable feeding, excellent flow properties, and consistent melting behavior. This reduces downtime caused by clogs or inconsistent feeding, allows faster production rates, and lowers scrap and reject rates. Manufacturers gain higher throughput and more reliable operations, even in complex extrusion or molding processes.

3. Applications Across the Plastics Industry

Bio Filler Masterbatch is highly versatile and can be used in a wide range of plastic products and processing techniques: 
  • Woven and Non-Woven Fabrics (PP/PE): Improves fiber stability, reduces breakage, and enhances surface quality.
  • Film and Sheet Extrusion: Replaces part of virgin polymer while maintaining transparency, tensile strength, and uniformity.
  • Injection Molding and Compounding: Ensures consistent filler dispersion, reduces warpage, and improves mechanical properties.
  • Composite and Bioplastic Materials: Supports sustainable material design without compromising stiffness, strength, or thermal resistance.
By using Bio Filler Masterbatch, manufacturers can produce plastics that are consistent, reliable, and sustainable, meeting modern industrial and environmental standards.

4. Role in Sustainable Production

Bio Filler Masterbatch helps manufacturers: 
  • Reduce environmental impact by decreasing the use of virgin plastics
  • Comply with eco-friendly regulations and standards
  • Offer products appealing to environmentally conscious consumers
  • Contribute to a circular economy with renewable or biodegradable fillers
This solution balances cost efficiency, product quality, and sustainability, making it a key tool for modern plastic manufacturing.

5. Conclusion

In conclusion, Bio Filler Masterbatch provides manufacturers with a holistic solution that enhances product quality, reduces material costs, improves production efficiency, and supports sustainability initiatives. By using Bio Filler Masterbatch, companies can produce high-performance plastics that meet both industrial and environmental standards, while minimizing production issues and maximizing efficiency.  For manufacturers seeking comprehensive solutions for plastic production, Mascom Global offers a wide range of Masterbatch solutions, including Filler Masterbatch, Color Masterbatch, and Additive Masterbatch, tailored for diverse applications such as injection molding, film blowing, sheet extrusion, and compounding. With our products, companies can optimize performance, reduce costs, and advance their sustainability goals, making Mascom Global a reliable partner for modern plastic manufacturing.

item.title: An Overview of Global Plastic and Masterbatch Trends 2026 – 2030
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Executive summary From 2026 to 2030, the global plastics market is expected to continue growing moderately while undergoing structural change: higher share of recycled and bio-based feedstocks, stronger regulatory pressure on single-use plastics, and faster adoption of circular technologies (mechanical + chemical recycling). The masterbatch market — color, filler and additive masterbatches — will expand in parallel, supported by packaging, automotive and construction demand, with sustainable and specialty masterbatches (bio-based, recyclable-compatible, additive masterbatches for advanced recycling) showing the fastest growth.  

Key market numbers & forecasts 

  • Global plastics market (value): recent industry estimates put the global plastics market at several hundred billion USD in 2023 and project ~4–5% CAGR toward 2030 (Grand View Research estimates ~4.3% CAGR to 2030). This growth is driven by packaging, medical devices and construction. 
  • Global masterbatch market: reputable market reports estimate the masterbatch market at roughly USD 6.6–12.4 billion (different definitions/reporting bases) with a mid-single digit CAGR (~4.5–6.6%) to 2030; most estimates converge on continued steady growth into 2030. (Grand View Research: USD 6.60B in 2024 → USD 9.65B by 2030 at ~6.6% CAGR; Mordor estimates ~4.5% CAGR). 
  • Advanced/chemical recycling capacity: capacity and investment in chemical recycling are accelerating rapidly (some reports projecting >25% CAGR for advanced recycling capacity in the late 2020s). This will materially affect feedstock availability and masterbatch formulations (compatibility with r-polymers). (Credit: GlobeNewswire)
Takeaway: Expect steady volume growth for masterbatch (low- to mid-single digit CAGR broadly), while premium/sustainable masterbatch segments grow faster. 

Structural drivers shaping 2026–2030 

Regulatory & sustainability pressure (circularity) 

  • Governments and brand owners will tighten requirements on recyclability, recycled content mandates and single-use plastic restrictions. This pushes converters to seek masterbatches that improve recyclability (compatibilizers, low-impact pigments, additives that do not impede recycling streams). 
  • Demand for bio-based and biodegradable masterbatch is rising (specialty segment growth reported above market average). (Credit: LinkedIn)

Recycling technologies and feedstock shifts 

  • Mechanical recycling remains primary, but chemical recycling (pyrolysis, depolymerization, solvent/enzymatic routes) is scaling rapidly; outputs (r-monomers, pyrolysis oils) will create new grades of recycled resins requiring tailored masterbatches (compatibility / dispersion). (Credit: GlobeNewswire+1)

Demand mix — packaging, automotive, construction 

  • Packaging continues to be the largest end-use; lighter gauge films, multi-layer structures and printed packaging will drive demand for color* and functional* masterbatches (antiblock, slip, anti-fog, UV). Automotive and construction will push higher-performance engineering masterbatches (flame retardants, thermal stabilizers, impact modifiers). (Grand View Research) 

Regional dynamics — Asia Pacific leadership 

  • Asia Pacific (China, India, Southeast Asia) will remain the largest growth region for masterbatch manufacturing and consumption due to downstream plastic conversion capacity expansion. Vietnam, Indonesia and India are notable growth markets for exporters. (Mordor Intelligence) 

Segment outlook — what will grow fastest (2026 – 2030) 

  1. Sustainable masterbatches (bio-based color/filler, biodegradable compatibilizers): above-market CAGR as brands require lower carbon footprint materials. (LinkedIn) 
  2. Masterbatches for recycled polymers (r-resins): formulations that improve dispersion, mechanical properties and color control in high-r content resins. 
  3. Functional/additive masterbatches (antimicrobial, anti-fog, UV stabilizers, flame retardants) — demand tied to higher-value end uses (medical, automotive, agriculture). 
  4. Standard color & filler masterbatches: steady base demand, price-sensitive; growth correlated with overall plastics production and packaging demand. (Grand View Research+1) 

Risks & headwinds (what could slow growth) 

  • Feedstock volatility & geopolitics: tariff changes, petrochemical overcapacity or feedstock supply disruptions can compress margins (recent trade/tariff actions have already pressured petrochemical players). (Credit: Reuters) 
  • Overcapacity in plastics & feedstock markets: may drive price competition and consolidation in masterbatch sector. 
  • Regulatory bans on certain additives or imposition of recycled content rules that are hard to meet quickly. 

Practical implications for masterbatch manufacturers (strategy & R&D priorities) 

  1. Invest in R&D for r-polymer compatibility: design masterbatches that preserve mechanical and optical properties when used with high-r content PE/PP/PET. 
  2. Launch sustainable product lines: bio-based carriers, low-impact pigments, and masterbatches formulated for chemical/mechanical recycling streams. 
  3. Quality & testing capability: expand lab capabilities (DSC, TGA, MFI, spectrophotometer, rheology) to certify performance on recycled feedstocks. 
  4. Value-added services: color matching, technical on-site support, small MOQ custom runs — differentiation versus commodity suppliers. 
  5. Collaborate upstream & downstream: partnerships with recyclers, resin producers and brand owners to co-develop solutions meeting regulatory specs and recyclability requirements. (Credit: Plastic Energy+1) 

Data-led forecasts & scenario view (simple model) 

Based on consensus report ranges, a reasonable scenario for masterbatch market 2026 – 2030: 
  • Base case: global masterbatch market grows at ~5–6% CAGR (2026 – 2030), reaching roughly USD 9–16 B by 2030 depending on baseline used (reports vary by segmentation & definition). (Credit: Grand View Research+1) 
  • Upside (rapid recycling & premium adoption): premium/sustainable masterbatches outperform (10%+ CAGR) and increase average ASPs (selling prices) due to value-added properties. 
  • Downside (feedstock shock / policy contraction): growth could compress below 3% CAGR in short windows if petrochemical margins & resin supply materially disrupt downstream conversion.

Conclusion 

Between 2026 and 2030 the masterbatch sector will keep growing steadily in volume, but the fastest commercial opportunities will be in sustainable & recycled-compatible masterbatches and functional/additive products. Manufacturers that combine R&D, testing infrastructure, and close collaboration with recyclers and converters will capture premium growth and mitigate margin pressure from commoditization.

item.title: Top Wire & Cable Trade Shows in Vietnam and Around the World 2025
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In the context of the rapidly growing wire and cable industry, attending specialized trade exhibitions has become an important opportunity for manufacturers, suppliers, and end-users to gain knowledge, explore new technologies, expand markets, and establish international collaborations. Below are some prominent exhibitions in 2025 that businesses in the wire and cable sector should not miss. 

1. Wire & Cable Show Vietnam 2025 (Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam – November 19 –21, 2025) This international exhibition for electrical equipment, wires and cables will be held at the Saigon Exhibition & Convention Center (SECC), District 7, Ho Chi Minh City. This is the 9th edition of the show and is regarded as the largest specialized event in Vietnam for the wire and cable industry. The exhibition gathers booths from both Vietnamese and international companies, showcasing electrical cables (special cables, underground cables, communication cables), optical fibers, cable manufacturing machinery, accessories, and materials.

Highlights: 
  • Connects the supply chain from R&D and design to production and application, providing opportunities for Vietnamese companies to integrate internationally. 
  • Focuses on trends such as renewable energy, power transmission, and automation. 
  • Targets manufacturers, contractors, end-users, and distributors, helping to find partners and expand in the ASEAN market. 
With its scale and influence in Vietnam, this event is highly recommended for wire and cable manufacturers, machinery factories, and suppliers of materials and accessories to update technologies and explore business opportunities. 

2. WireShow 2025 – The 12th China International Wire and Cable Industry Exhibition (Shanghai, China – August 27–29, 2025) Held in Shanghai, this large-scale exhibition spans approximately 57,500 m² and features over 750 exhibitors from China and abroad. The event focuses on wires and cables, manufacturing machinery, auxiliary materials, testing and measurement technologies, special cables, and optical fibers.

Highlights: 
  • A major hub for the wire and cable industry in Asia, allowing participants to update modern production technologies, automation, and new material solutions. 
  • Suitable for companies seeking to expand into the Chinese market or source advanced machinery. 
  • Includes in-depth seminars and expert networking sessions to better understand technical trends in the industry. 

3. Wire Southeast Asia 2025 (Bangkok, Thailand – September 17–19, 2025) Organized by Messe Düsseldorf Asia at the BITEC Center in Bangkok, this is the largest wire and cable exhibition in Southeast Asia. The show attracts over 400 exhibitors from more than 30 countries and territories.

Highlights: 
  • Convenient for Vietnamese businesses due to lower costs compared to Europe or North America, while maintaining international exposure. 
  • Focuses on wire processing machinery, cable manufacturing equipment, and solutions for the rapidly growing regional wire and cable industry. 
  • Provides opportunities to connect with ASEAN companies, expand export markets, or find production partners. 

4. Cable & Wire Fair 2025 (New Delhi, India – November 4–6, 2025)

Now in its 6th edition, this exhibition in New Delhi is a key destination in South Asia. The event focuses on wires and cables for power transmission, telecommunications, materials, and manufacturing machinery. Highlights: 
  • In a large market like India, businesses can tap into significant domestic demand for electricity, telecommunications, and infrastructure. 
  • Meet manufacturers and distributors in South Asia and the Middle East to expand international networks. 
  • Accompanied by specialized conferences to update industry trends, such as high-voltage power transmission, optical fibers, and insulating materials. 

Conclusion and Recommendations for Vietnamese Businesses

Overall, these exhibitions are not only platforms for product display, but also foundations for companies in the wire and cable industry to update technology, find partners, expand markets, and understand global trends. For Vietnamese companies involved in cable manufacturing, machinery, or ancillary services, attending at least one or two events in 2025 is highly recommended.  To maximize effectiveness at exhibitions, companies should: 
  • Set clear goals (market expansion, machinery acquisition, finding production partners, sourcing materials) before attending. 
  • Prepare documents, product samples, technology information, and production capabilities for presentation at the booth. 
  • Participate in side seminars/forums to gain deeper market and technical insights. 
  • Follow up with contacts made at the exhibition to convert successful meetings into real collaborations. 
Finally, as the wire and cable industry becomes increasingly competitive and demands higher quality in materials, automation, and sustainability, participating in international exhibitions is an effective strategy to maintain and expand competitive advantages. We wish your business success and fruitful connections at the wire and cable events in 2025!

item.title: PP Reprocessed Granules: Composition, Uses & Application Methods
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In the plastics industry, PP Reprocessed Granules have become an economical, efficient, and environmentally friendly solution. These recycled plastic granules not only help reduce raw material costs, but also minimize plastic waste, opening up a wide range of applications in modern plastic manufacturing. To use them effectively, manufacturers must understand the nature, composition, uses, and proper application methods of recycled PP.

1️⃣ What Are PP Reprocessed Granules?

PP Reprocessed Granules are polypropylene pellets recovered from post-consumer plastic products or production scrap. These pellets undergo recycling, cleaning, grinding, and re-extrusion into uniform granules, ready to be used in new plastic products. Compared to virgin PP, recycled PP may contain residual fillers or additives, so it is essential to evaluate mechanical properties, thermal stability, and overall quality before production. Key benefits include:
  • Reducing raw material costs compared to virgin PP, typically 10 – 30% savings depending on the source and blend ratio.
  • Supporting green manufacturing goals and environmental sustainability.
  • Suitable for a wide range of plastic applications that do not require high mechanical performance, such as films, containers, interior parts, packaging, and fibers.

2️⃣ Composition of PP Reprocessed Granules

A standard batch of PP reprocessed granules usually consists of:
  1. Polypropylene base (PP): about 80 – 95%, depending on the source material.
  2. Optional fillers: such as CaCO₃, talc, or silica, which increase stiffness, reduce shrinkage, and lower production costs.
  3. Residual additives: UV stabilizers, antioxidants, lubricants, and colorants from previous products.
  4. Low moisture content (<0.3%): Recycled PP must be dried before injection, extrusion, or blow molding to ensure product quality.
🔹 Note: The quality of recycled PP largely depends on the source material and recycling process. Reliable sources ensure performance close to virgin PP.

3️⃣ Applications of PP Reprocessed Granules

PP Reprocessed Granules are versatile and cost-effective, suitable for multiple plastic applications:
Application Purpose / Use
Injection Molding Manufacturing plastic boxes, trays, household items, and industrial components.
Extrusion Film / Sheet Agricultural films, packaging films, liner films.
Blow Molding Bottles, cans, drums, and containers.
PP Woven Sack / Raffia Fibers for woven sacks, agricultural and industrial packaging.
Non-Woven Fabric Fibers for bags, non-woven textiles, and filtration materials.
Advantages of using recycled PP:
  • 💰 Cost savings in raw material and overall production.
  • ♻️ Environmentally friendly, reducing plastic waste.
  • ⚙️ Easily blended with virgin resin or filler masterbatch to enhance mechanical properties when needed.

4️⃣ How to Use PP Reprocessed Granules

To achieve optimal performance, follow these steps when using recycled PP:
  1. Dry the granules before processing: recommended drying temperature is 80 – 90°C for 4 – 6 hours to reduce moisture content.
  2. Blend with virgin PP: common ratios are 20 to 50% recycled PP + 50 to 80% virgin PP, balancing cost savings and mechanical performance.
  3. Add fillers or additives if necessary: to increase stiffness, reduce shrinkage, enhance UV stability, or prevent static.
  4. Control processing temperature and screw speed: recycled PP may contain impurities, and excessive heat can cause oxidation or color changes.
  5. Conduct trial runs before full-scale production: assess flexibility, mechanical strength, color, and dispersibility to determine the optimal blend.

5️⃣ Practical Operation & Testing Considerations

  • Source control: Choose recycled PP granules with a clear origin, high purity, and good dispersibility.
  • Small batch trials: Evaluate mechanical properties, flexibility, color, printability, and film drawability.
  • Adjust blend formulations: For products requiring higher strength, increase virgin PP ratio or add filler masterbatch.
  • Monitor extrusion or molding process: Adjust temperature, screw speed, and pressure to prevent hot spots, deformation, or air voids.
  • Regular quality evaluation: Monitor strength, flexibility, gloss, and dispersibility to ensure the final product meets technical specifications.

🌍 Conclusion

PP Reprocessed Granules offer a smart, cost-effective, and sustainable solution for the plastics industry. When sourced from reliable suppliers and used correctly, recycled PP can deliver performance close to virgin PP, reduce production costs, and contribute to environmental protection. At Mascom Global, we provide high-quality PP Reprocessed Granules, strictly controlled for mechanical performance, moisture content, and dispersibility, helping customers achieve optimal results across all plastic applications. 🌟 Mascom Global – Real Value Commitment. Contact us today for detailed technical consultation and tailored solutions for PP Reprocessed Granules.

item.title: PE Taical vs. PP Taical: Differences
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In the plastics industry — where cost optimization, productivity, and product quality are constantly pushed to higher standards — Filler Masterbatch a.k.a Taical (CaCO₃- based) has become an indispensable material. Among the most widely used types today are PE Taical and PP Taical. Though both share a common CaCO₃ foundation, their properties and performance differ significantly.  Understanding these differences is essential for manufacturers aiming to reduce raw material costs, improve production efficiency, and enhance end-product quality.  Drawing from practical experience at Mascom Global — a leading producer of Filler Masterbatch trusted by factories across Asia, Europe, the Americas, and Africa — this article provides an in-depth comparison to help you choose the right filler for your specific application.

1. Overview of PE Taical and PP Taical

1.1 PE Taical  

PE Taical (PE Filler Masterbatch CaCO3) is produced from a Polyethylene base resin (LDPE, LLDPE, or HDPE), CaCO₃ powder, and suitable additives.  Advantages: 
  • Low processing temperature 
  • High flexibility 
  • Smooth surface 
  • Excellent dispersion in soft and flexible film applications 

1.2 PP Taical  

PP Taical (PP Filler Masterbatch CaCO3) uses a Polypropylene base resin combined with CaCO₃ and additives, making it ideal for applications requiring higher stiffness and tensile strength.  Advantages: 
  • Superior tensile strength 
  • High rigidity 
  • Excellent thermal stability 
  • Suitable for high-speed stretching and extrusion processes 
Mascom Global leverages these characteristics to produce customized Filler Masterbatch grades for blown film, PP nonwoven, raffia, PP injection molding, industrial films, and more. 

2. Detailed Comparison of PE Taical vs. PP Taical

2.1 Mechanical Properties 

Mechanical Property  PE Taical  PP Taical 
Flexibility  High  Medium – Low 
Tensile Strength  Good  Excellent 
Stiffness  Low  High 
Impact Resistance  Good  Moderate 
➡ PP Taical suits rigid products requiring high strength. ➡ PE Taical is ideal for soft, thin, flexible films. 

2.2 Processing Performance 

Processing Factor  PE Taical  PP Taical 
Processing Temperature  Low  High 
Extrusion Speed  High  Very High 
Energy Consumption  Low  Medium 
Thermal Stability  Medium  High 
Mascom Global’s advanced European-standard production lines ensure: 
  • Lower extrusion pressure 
  • Reduced friction 
  • Excellent CaCO₃ dispersion 
  • 8 – 12% higher output 
  • 5 – 10% lower energy consumption 

2.3 Polymer Compatibility 

  • PE Taical → LDPE, LLDPE, HDPE, EVA 
  • PP Taical → PP raffia, PP injection molding, PP film, PP sheet 
Incorrect selection can lead to: 
  • Surface micro-voids 
  • Reduced strength 
  • Hazy films 
  • Raffia yarn breakage 
  • Poor dispersion 
Mascom Global prevents these issues by using 100% virgin PE/PP carrier resins, ensuring perfect compatibility with CaCO₃ particles. 

2.4 Surface Quality & Optical Properties 

Property  PE Taical  PP Taical 
Gloss  Good  Very Good 
Smoothness  Excellent  Good 
Shrinkage Stability  Good  Excellent 
➡ PP fillers deliver a glossier, harder surface. ➡ PE fillers deliver smoother, more flexible film surfaces. 

2.5 Economic Benefits 

The primary benefit of Filler Masterbatch is reducing virgin resin consumption while maintaining or improving product performance. 
  • In raffia applications, high-quality PP Taical can be used at up to 50% loading without loss of strength — an advantage strongly demonstrated by Mascom Global’s PP grades. 
  • In blown film, PE Taical can also be used at high loading levels (up to or above 50%) while preserving film quality. 

3. Applications of PE Taical and PP Taical

3.1 PE Taical Applications 

  • LDPE/LLDPE/HDPE blown film 
  • Shopping bags, garbage bags 
  • Agricultural film 
  • PE flexible hoses 
  • Industrial films 
  • Bottles and containers 
➡ Best for soft, flexible, thin film products. 

3.2 PP Taical Applications 

  • Raffia yarn 
  • Woven sacks 
  • PP hollow sheets 
  • PP injection molding 
  • PP film 
  • PP nonwoven 
➡ Ideal for rigid, strong products and high-speed stretching processes.  Mascom Global provides application-specific grades ensuring: 
  • Reduced yarn breakage 
  • Stripe-free films 
  • Smooth surfaces 
  • Higher output 
  • Consistent dispersion 

4. Should You Choose PE Taical or PP Taical?

Choose PE Taical if you need: 
  • Soft, flexible products 
  • Smooth surface finish 
  • Low-temperature processing 
  • Blown film or thin bag applications 
Choose PP Taical if you need: 
  • High tensile strength 
  • Rigid, glossy surfaces 
  • Dimensional stability 
  • High-speed raffia or extrusion 
Mascom Global supports customers by recommending the right filler based on: 
  • Product requirements 
  • Machine configuration 
  • Line speed 
  • Optimal dosing ratio 

5. What Makes Mascom Global’s Taical Different?

Mascom Global is highly trusted for its: 
  • Ultra-fine CaCO₃ with >98% purity 
  • Advanced surface treatment for perfect dispersion 
  • 100% virgin PE/PP carrier resin 
  • Consistent quality in every batch 
  • Experienced technical team offering strong on-site support 
Real-world customer results: 
  • 8 – 12% higher productivity 
  • 5 – 10% less energy consumption 
  • Improved surface appearance 
  • Lower defect rate 
  • Less machine and die cleaning required 

6. Conclusion

Both PE Taical and PP Taical provide significant economic and technical advantages. The key to maximizing performance is selecting the correct carrier resin and application-specific grade. With premium CaCO₃ sources, modern production technologies, and expert technical support, Mascom Global is committed to delivering optimized Filler Masterbatch solutions — helping manufacturers boost output, reduce costs, and maintain stable long-term quality.

item.title: What is Flexible PVC Compound and Applications
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
1. What is Flexible PVC Compound?

Flexible PVC Compound is a type of PVC that has been blended with plasticizers, stabilizers, fillers, and other additives to create a material that is flexible, elastic, and easier to process compared to rigid PVC Compound.  By incorporating plasticizers, Flexible PVC can be bent, stretched, or molded without cracking, while maintaining mechanical strength, chemical resistance, and weather durability. The product is typically produced in the form of compound pellets, ready for extrusion, molding, film blowing, calendering, or other processing methods.

2. Key Components of Flexible PVC Compound

Flexible PVC Compound consists of several components, each contributing to the material’s performance: 

2.1. PVC Resin 

  • Serves as the base material, providing mechanical strength and structural integrity.
  • Available in fine powder or pellet form, influencing surface smoothness and processability.

2.2. Plasticizers 

  • Provide flexibility and softness to PVC.
  • Common types include DOP (Dioctyl Phthalate), DINP, DIDP, TOTM.
  • The proportion of plasticizer typically ranges from 20 – 60% by weight of PVC, determining flexibility and elongation.
  • Applications in medical or food-contact products require non-toxic, safe plasticizers.

2.3. Stabilizers 

  • Prevent thermal, oxidative, or UV degradation of PVC.
  • Common types include calcium-zinc stabilizers, organic stabilizers, and mixed metal stabilizers.
  • Help maintain color stability, prevent yellowing, and extend product life.

2.4. Fillers 

  • Reduce cost and enhance mechanical properties, such as CaCO₃, talc, mica.
  • Improve rigidity, tensile strength, and processing performance.
  • Typical filler content varies by application: 5 – 40% for films, higher for pipes or sheets requiring strength.

2.5. Pigments & Additives 

  • Pigments: Provide desired color and aesthetic finish.
  • Additives: Include UV stabilizers, anti-static agents, flame retardants, lubricants, and processing aids.
  • Essential for surface quality, environmental resistance, and long-term performance.

3. Key Features of Flexible PVC Compound

  • High Flexibility: Can be bent, stretched, or molded without cracking.
  • Thermal and Chemical Resistance: Stable under mild heat and chemical exposure.
  • UV and Weather Resistance: Suitable for outdoor applications.
  • Ease of Processing: Can be extruded, molded, calendered, blown, or used for wires and tubing.
  • Color Customization: Easy to color according to specific application requirements.

4. Applications of Flexible PVC Compound

Flexible PVC Compound is widely used across multiple industries due to its flexibility, durability, and customizable properties. 

4.1. Construction Industry 

  • Flexible Pipes and Floor Drains: High mechanical strength, pressure-resistant, and easy to install.
  • Flooring, Roofing Sheets, and Waterproof Membranes: Provide wear resistance, slip resistance, and weather durability.
  • Electrical Wires & Cables: Flexible insulation, fire-resistant, and long-lasting.

4.2. Medical Industry 

  • Tubing and IV Bags: Non-toxic, soft, kink-resistant, and safe for medical use.
  • PVC Gloves: Flexible, comfortable, and durable for healthcare applications.

4.3. Packaging and Agriculture 

  • Flexible Packaging Films and Bags: Protect food, chemicals, or medical supplies.
  • Waterproof Sheets and Agricultural Films: Durable, weather-resistant, and tear-resistant for outdoor use.

4.4. Automotive and Electronics 

  • Flexible Hoses and Wiring: Heat-resistant, abrasion-resistant, and electrically insulated.
  • Protective Sheathing for Cables and Components: Flexible, durable, and easy to install.

5. Benefits of Using Flexible PVC Compound

  • Cost-effective Production: Easy extrusion, molding, and blowing reduce material loss.
  • Extended Product Life: Resistant to cracking, breaking, and mechanical stress.
  • Customizable Properties: Flexibility, color, UV resistance, flame retardancy, and hardness can be adjusted according to requirements.
  • Versatile Applications: Suitable for construction, medical, packaging, automotive, and electronics industries.

6. Considerations When Using Flexible PVC Compound

  • Choose the Right Plasticizer: Ensure safety and suitability for the intended application, especially in medical or food-contact products.
  • Control Processing Temperature: Avoid overheating to prevent PVC degradation.
  • Proper Storage: Protect from moisture, direct sunlight, and high temperatures to maintain

7. Conclusion 

Flexible PVC Compound is a versatile and flexible plastic solution widely used across various industries. Selecting the right compound and combining it with appropriate processing technology ensures optimal performance, durability, and cost efficiency.  At Mascom Global, we provide high-quality Flexible PVC Compounds, customized to meet customer requirements, supporting manufacturers in construction, medical, packaging, automotive, and electronics industries. With extensive experience and modern production facilities, we are committed to delivering consistent products, optimal solutions, and dedicated support, helping our clients improve productivity, reduce costs, and maintain superior product quality.

item.title: Types of Bio Plastics and Applications in Bio Compound Production
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
With increasing global awareness of environmental protection and stricter regulations on single-use plastics, bio-based and biodegradable plastics have become an essential alternative to conventional petrochemical materials. Not only European and Americas countries recommend to use these biodegradable and alternative products. Nowadays, many countries in Asia, Africa, Middle East etc encourage to replace products from virgin plastic by bio-plastics or paper products    These Bio Plastics are derived from renewable resources such as corn starch, sugarcane, or cassava, offering a lower carbon footprint and improved end-of-life options through compostability or biodegradability. Below is some common bio plastics and it’s applications in plastic industry  

1. Main Types of Bio Plastics

1.1 PLA (Polylactic Acid) 

  • Produced from fermented plant starch (commonly corn or cassava).
  • Biodegradable under industrial composting conditions.
  • Eco-friendly: A more sustainable alternative to petroleum-based plastics.
  • Good mechanical properties: Offers moderate strength, rigidity, and stiffness, though this can be modified.
  • High gloss and clarity: Comparable to PET, making it good for aesthetically pleasing products.
  • Food safe: Generally regarded as safe for food contact due to its non-toxic breakdown products.
  • Easy to process: Has good workability
Applications: food packaging, disposable tableware, thermoformed trays, and 3D printing filament.

1.2 PBAT (Polybutylene Adipate Terephthalate) 

  • A biodegradable polymer known for its flexibility and toughness, similar to
  • Often blended with PLA or starch to improve mechanical and processing properties.
  • It has relatively low tensile strength, but this can be improved by blending with other polymers. 
  • The cost of raw materials for PBAT is relatively high, making it more expensive than traditional plastics.
  • Barrier Properties: It has a high oxygen permeation but a lower water vapor permeability compared to some other bioplastics
Applications: compostable shopping bags, agricultural films, and flexible packaging.

1.3 PBS / PBSA (Polybutylene Succinate / Polybutylene Succinate Adipate) 

  • Derived partly from renewable feedstock.
  • Combines biodegradability with good heat and chemical resistance.
  • Mechanical Properties: PBS has good strength and ductility, while PBSA is known for its flexibility. These properties can be enhanced by blending with other materials or adding fillers.
  • Biodegradation Pathway: PBS degrades into low-molecular-weight polymers when exposed to water, with the rate increasing with temperature.
  • Customizable Properties: The properties of PBS and its copolymers can be tailored by changing the composition, such as adding adipic acid to create PBSA.
Applications: extrusion films, coffee capsules, coated paper, injection molding, and thermoforming and agricultural mulch films.

1.4 PHA (Polyhydroxyalkanoates) 

  • 100% bio-based and fully biodegradable in soil and marine environments.
  • Versatility: The properties of PHAs can be customized by altering the microorganism and fermentation conditions 
  • Renewable source: PHAs are derived from renewable resources, aligning with the principles of a circular bioeconomy.
  • Barrier properties: Some PHAs exhibit excellent barrier properties
Applications: cosmetic and medical packaging, marine products, and single-use items.

2. What is a Bio Compound?

A Bio Compound is a custom-engineered material that combines bio-based resins (like PLA, PBAT, PBS, or PHA) with selected additives, fillers, or biodegradable masterbatch to enhance mechanical, thermal, and processing performance.  Bio Compounds help manufacturers achieve: 
  • Improved strength and flexibility for end products.
  • Optimized processability for film blowing, injection, or extrusion applications.
  • Cost-effectiveness through material blending.
  • Reduced environmental impact and compliance with green standards.

3. Applications of Bio Compounds

Bio Compounds are widely used in: 
  • Compostable shopping and garbage bags
  • Agricultural mulch films
  • Disposable food containers and cutlery
  • 3D printing filaments
  • Paper coating and lamination layers

item.title: Essential Certifications and Compliance Requirements for Plastic Products Manufactured for Food Contact
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In today’s global marketplace, food safety is a top priority for consumers, regulators, and manufacturers alike. Plastic products designed for food contact — such as containers, packaging films, bottles, utensils, and kitchenware — must undergo strict assessments to ensure they do not pose health risks. To guarantee compliance, businesses must obtain a series of certifications and follow regulatory standards that verify the product’s safety, quality, and suitability for food use. Below are some of the most important certifications and testing requirements for plastic products intended for food contact applications.

1. FDA Compliance (U.S. Market)

For companies exporting to or operating within the United States, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) plays a central role in regulating food contact materials. Plastics must comply with FDA 21 CFR regulations, which outline the types of polymers, additives, stabilizers, and processing aids that are permitted for contact with food. FDA compliance does not require a physical certificate issued by the government; instead, manufacturers must perform appropriate testing and maintain documentation demonstrating that the materials meet FDA requirements. This ensures that no harmful substances migrate into food and that the product is safe under normal conditions of use.

2. EU Regulation (Europe Market): EC No. 1935/2004 & EU 10/2011

Europe enforces some of the strictest regulations for food contact materials. Two key frameworks include:
  • Regulation (EC) No. 1935/2004 – This sets general safety requirements for all food contact materials, ensuring that products do not transfer substances that could endanger health, change food composition, or alter its sensory properties.
  • EU Regulation 10/2011 – This is specific to plastics and establishes the Union List, which identifies substances allowed in the manufacturing of plastic food-contact materials. It requires migration testing, including overall migration limits (OML) and specific migration limits (SML) for certain substances.
Manufacturers must also provide a Declaration of Compliance (DoC), summarizing test results and confirming conformity with applicable EU laws.

3. LFGB Certification (German Standard)

Germany’s LFGB (Lebensmittel-, Bedarfsgegenstände- und Futtermittelgesetzbuch) is widely respected for its rigorous testing standards. Products carrying the LFGB mark or “knife and fork” symbol demonstrate high safety levels and compliance with German laws governing food contact materials. LFGB testing often includes:
  • Sensory testing
  • Chemical safety assessments
  • Migration tests
  • Heavy metal testing
Because of its strictness, LFGB certification is often used as a selling point for brands wanting to position their products as safe and premium-quality.

4. ISO Certifications for Quality and Safety Management

Although ISO certifications do not directly approve food contact materials, they reinforce the manufacturer’s commitment to consistent quality and safety management. Important ISO standards include:
  • ISO 9001 – Quality management system
  • ISO 22000 – Food safety management (especially relevant for food packaging manufacturers)
  • ISO 14001 – Environmental management
Holding these certifications strengthens consumer trust and demonstrates comprehensive control over production processes.

ISO 9001:2015 Certificate - Mascom Global

5. RoHS and REACH Compliance

For manufacturers selling in Europe and other international markets, RoHS and REACH may also apply:
  • RoHS (Restriction of Hazardous Substances) ensures that products do not contain unsafe levels of heavy metals such as lead, cadmium, mercury, or chromium VI.
  • REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation, and Restriction of Chemicals) requires manufacturers to identify chemical substances used in production and limit exposure to harmful chemicals.
While these regulations mainly target electronics and industrial materials, many food-grade plastic components, especially multi-purpose plastics, must also comply.

REACH Certificate - Mascom Global

6. SGS, Intertek, and TÜV Testing Reports

In addition to mandatory regulatory compliance, many businesses choose reputable third-party labs such as SGS, Intertek, or TÜV to conduct independent testing. These organizations provide:
  • Migration and chemical safety tests
  • Heavy metal content assessments
  • Temperature resistance testing
  • BPA-free or phthalate-free validation
These reports enhance brand credibility and help partners or distributors evaluate product safety more easily.

Conclusion

For plastic products manufactured for food contact, certifications are not only a legal requirement — they are a guarantee of consumer protection and a foundation for building market trust. Whether targeting the U.S., EU, or global markets, complying with FDA regulations, EU standards, LFGB requirements, ISO systems, and additional chemical safety regulations ensures that plastic products meet the highest levels of safety and quality. Investing in proper certification processes ultimately strengthens a brand’s reputation and supports long-term success in the competitive food packaging and kitchenware industry.
