A Cast Film Extruder is a type of plastic film extrusion machine that operates by forcing molten plastic through a flat slot die, after which the film is immediately cooled on chill rollers. Compared to blown film extrusion, cast film extrusion offers several advantages:
  • The film is shaped on a flat surface rather than blown into a tubular form.
  • Film thickness is highly uniform, with a smooth and glossy surface.
  • Films can be produced in thin, medium, or thick gauges depending on the application.
Advantages of cast film extrusion:
  • Produces films with stable thickness and surface quality.
  • High production speed and throughput.
  • Easily compatible with coatings, surface treatments, or additional additives.

2️⃣ What is PVC Compound and Its Role in Cast Film Extrusion?

PVC Compound is a mixture of virgin PVC resin with plasticizers, stabilizers, fillers, lubricants, and other additives. It is designed to optimize flexibility, heat resistance, impact strength, and color stability during processing. In cast film extrusion, PVC Compound plays a key role:
  • Provides flexibility and mechanical strength to the film.
  • Stabilizes the extrusion process, reducing shrinkage and deformation.
  • Enhances the dispersion of fillers and additives, ensuring uniform, smooth, and glossy films.
  • Adjusts surface properties, such as anti-stick, anti-static, printability, or UV protection.

3️⃣ Benefits of Using PVC Compound for Cast Film Extrusion

Using high-quality PVC Compound allows manufacturers to:
  • Improve film quality: achieve uniform thickness, smooth glossy surfaces, and free from bubbles or pinholes.
  • Increase productivity and operational stability: stable extrusion reduces downtime caused by clogging or film deformation.
  • Optimize material costs: combine fillers or masterbatches to lower production costs while maintaining film performance.
  • Diversify product offerings: easy to color, add UV or anti-static layers, suitable for food packaging, agricultural films, construction films, and more.

4️⃣ Guidelines for Using PVC Compound in Cast Film Extruders

To achieve optimal results, the following considerations are important:
  1. Choose the right PVC Compound:
    • Select a compound with appropriate flexibility and processing temperature for your extruder.
    • Consider filler, plasticizer, and stabilizer ratios to meet mechanical requirements.
  2. Dry the material before extrusion:
    • Proper drying reduces moisture content, preventing bubbles or voids in the film.
  3. Control extrusion temperature and screw speed:
    • Excessive temperature may degrade the plastic or discolor the film.
    • Too low a temperature can cause clogging or uneven films.
    • Adjust screw speed to achieve the desired film thickness.
  4. Use chill rollers correctly:
    • Ensure even cooling to maintain flatness and avoid shrinkage.
    • Roller temperature should be uniform across the width to prevent curling or waves.
  5. Regular testing and evaluation:
    • Measure thickness, gloss, tensile strength, and uniformity.
    • Adjust PVC Compound formulation or extrusion parameters as needed to maintain consistent quality.

5️⃣ Common Applications of Cast Film Extrusion with PVC Compound

  • Agricultural films (agri-film): weather-resistant, UV-protected, moisture-retentive.
  • Food packaging films: transparent, flexible, food-safe.
  • Technical / construction films: heat and load-resistant, waterproof.
  • Industrial packaging films: PE/PVC blends for protecting goods during transport.

🌍 Mascom Global — High-Quality PVC Compound Solutions

Mascom Global provides high-quality PVC Compound in a wide range of types and applications, helping film manufacturers optimize performance, stabilize production, and enhance final product quality. With extensive experience in the masterbatch and PVC industry, Mascom is committed to supporting customers from material selection and formulation advice to operational guidance. Contact Mascom today to receive personalized PVC Compound solutions for your cast film extruder and maximize production efficiency and film quality!

1. What is Anti-fog Additive?
Anti-fog additive is a specialized additive used in plastic products to prevent water vapor from condensing into tiny droplets on the surface of films or plastic materials.  When plastic products (such as agricultural films, food packaging films, plastic trays, greenhouse films, etc.) are exposed to moisture and temperature fluctuations, water vapor often condenses on the surface into droplets – a phenomenon known as "fogging." This can obscure visibility, reduce light transmission efficiency, or affect the quality of the product inside.  Anti-fog additives work by reducing the surface energy of the plastic film, allowing water vapor to spread evenly as a thin, transparent layer rather than forming droplets. As a result, the surface remains clear and clean, enhancing both the aesthetic value and product quality.   
  1. Key Benefits of Anti-fog Additive

 In Agriculture (Greenhouse Films, Crop Cover Films): 

  • Improved light transmission: Allows more sunlight to pass through, promoting photosynthesis and increasing crop yields. 
  • Reduced heat loss: Prevents droplets from harming young plants, flowers, or fruits. 
  • Extended film lifespan: Reduces oxidation, mold, or dust accumulation caused by condensed moisture. 

 In Food Packaging (PE, PP, PET Films, Trays): 

  • Keeps packaging surfaces transparent and visually appealing, making products look fresh and attractive. 
  • Limits bacterial growth by reducing localized moisture on the packaging surface. 
  • Extends food shelf life, especially for fruits, vegetables, and fresh produce. 

 In Other Industrial Applications: 

  • Used for shrink films, laminated films, transparent sheets, plastic lids, etc., maintaining gloss, clarity, and stability in humid environments. 
 
  1. How to Use Anti-fog Additive in Plastic Manufacturing
Anti-fog additives are usually supplied in the form of masterbatch (concentrated resin pellets), which can be directly mixed with base resin during production.   Recommended usage rate: 
  • Typically 1% – 3%, depending on the type of plastic, film thickness, and application requirements. 
  • For thin films or products requiring high transparency, small-scale trials are recommended to determine the optimal ratio. 
 Usage notes: 
  • Ensure uniform mixing with the raw material before extrusion or molding. 
  • Maintain stable processing temperatures to ensure proper additive dispersion. 
  • Can be combined with other additives such as anti-static, slip, or anti-blocking agents to enhance overall product performance. 
 
  1. Additional Benefits and Long-term Impact
Beyond primary applications, anti-fog additives provide important benefits for improving production efficiency and reducing waste. When plastic films or products experience fogging, it not only affects aesthetics but also lowers product quality, increases defect rates, and complicates packaging and storage. With anti-fog additives, water droplets disperse evenly across the surface, reducing localized moisture and keeping products stable during transportation and storage.  Using anti-fog additives also contributes to environmental protection, as products maintain their quality longer, reducing replacement needs and plastic waste. In the food industry, these additives help extend shelf life without increasing chemical preservatives, while enhancing food safety and hygiene.  For manufacturers, anti-fog masterbatches integrate easily into existing processes, reducing trial times and optimizing costs. When combined with other additives like anti-static, slip, or anti-blocking agents, plastic products achieve higher overall performance, meeting technical and aesthetic requirements.  These advantages make anti-fog additives a comprehensive solution to improve quality, increase commercial value, and enhance the end-user experience across multiple industries.   
  1. Benefits of Using Mascom Global’s Anti-fog Masterbatch
Mascom Global provides specially formulated Anti-fog Masterbatches for various applications: 
  • Anti-fog for agricultural films (Greenhouse Film) 
  • Anti-fog for food packaging (Food Packaging Film) 
  • Anti-fog for transparent industrial applications (Transparent Film/Sheet) 
Outstanding advantages: ✅ Long-lasting anti-fog performance, stable under various temperature and humidity conditions. ✅ Uniform dispersion, without affecting film transparency or color. ✅ Compatible with multiple base resins: LDPE, LLDPE, PP, PET, EVA… ✅ Environmentally friendly, non-toxic, safe for food packaging.   
  1. Conclusion
Anti-fog additives are an effective solution to enhance the quality and value of plastic products across multiple sectors – from agriculture to food packaging and industrial applications. Using the right type and proportion not only ensures products remain durable and transparent but also optimizes production efficiency and user experience.  👉 Contact Mascom Global for advice on the most suitable Anti-fog Masterbatch solutions for your processes and applications.  Mascom Global – Real Value, Commitment. Delivering real value through real commitment.

PT Kasakata Kimia is a local manufacturer specializing in color masterbatch, functional masterbatch, and plastic additives. Kasakata is recognized as a key local supplier, especially for customers requiring customized colors and special effects.

Other manufacturers, such as Rainbow Masterbatch, are known for focusing on filler masterbatch (e.g., CaCO₃) for film, heavy-duty packaging, and construction products. The filler masterbatch market is growing in Southeast Asia due to its cost-saving potential while improving product mechanical properties. Specialized filler producers often collaborate closely with calcium carbonate suppliers and plastic manufacturers to optimize formulations.

5. Other Notable Local Manufacturers

In addition to major players, there are many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating effectively on a local scale, such as Khitas Masterbatch, and custom color mixing factories serving industrial clusters in Bekasi, Bandung, and Cikarang — major industrial areas in Java. These suppliers are often more flexible with smaller orders, provide direct technical support, and develop formulations quickly for OEM customers.

Market Trends and Brief Analysis

  • Rising demand for filler & low-cost masterbatch: Due to raw material cost pressures, many manufacturers are turning to filler (CaCO₃) to reduce plastic production costs while maintaining basic performance. Filler masterbatch producers in Indonesia and the region provide popular solutions for the packaging and fiber industries.
  • Diversification from color to functional masterbatch: Buyers increasingly demand masterbatch not only for color but also for functionality (UV stabilizer, antistatic, slip, flame retardant). This drives major manufacturers to invest in R&D. (polychemindo.com)
  • Presence of international brands: Global brands (e.g., foreign plants or brands cooperating or distributing in Indonesia) still have influence, creating competition in both technology and pricing. Market reports list many local and international players active in Indonesia. (MarkNtel Advisors)

Advice for Buyers / Importers

  • Verify production capacity: For large orders, prioritize manufacturers with automated production lines, quality control, and relevant certifications (physical-chemical, food safety if needed).
  • Request samples and audit factories: Always request samples and, when necessary, conduct audits to check blending processes and color consistency.
  • Consider smaller local suppliers: For small quantities or frequent color/formulation changes, local SMEs are often more flexible and have shorter lead times.

Conclusion

The masterbatch market in Indonesia includes large-scale industrial companies like Polychem, distribution-linked producers like Dunia Kimia Jaya (Lautan Luas), as well as specialized manufacturers like Kasakata, Rainbow Masterbatch, and Khitas. Depending on objectives (price, quality, quantity), buyers can choose between large manufacturers for consistency or local suppliers for flexibility. “As Indonesia’s masterbatch market continues to grow, Mascom stands out as a trusted partner, delivering high-quality color and filler masterbatches that help manufacturers optimize costs, enhance product performance, and lead in the industry. In practice, Mascom has successfully exported multiple shipments of filler masterbatch to the Indonesian market and received very positive feedback from local manufacturers regarding product consistency, smooth dispersion, and competitive pricing. These strong responses motivate us to continue improving our formulations and expanding product ranges to meet Indonesia’s needs — from thin film packaging and PP/PE woven sacks to high-output injection molding and blown film applications. In modern plastic manufacturing, plastic additives play a vital role in improving material performance, enhancing durability, and optimizing production costs. When using virgin polymers alone (PP, PE, ABS, PVC, etc.), the material often cannot fully meet requirements for mechanical strength, stability, processability, or aesthetics. Therefore, additives become essential solutions that help manufacturers elevate product quality and develop specialized material formulations for different applications.  Below is an overview of the most common groups of plastic additives, along with their functions and practical applications.   
  1. Antioxidants

Function 

Antioxidants protect polymers from degradation caused by heat, oxygen, and UV exposure during melt processing or end-use environments. 

Benefits 

  • Stabilizes color and reduces yellowing. 
  • Prevents polymer chain breaking, maintaining mechanical strength. 
  • Extends product lifespan, especially for outdoor applications. 

Applications 

  • LDPE, HDPE blown films. 
  • Packaging bags, T-shirt bags, shopping bags. 
  • Injection molded parts, plastic pipes, sheets. 
 
  1. UV Stabilizers (UV Absorbers / HALS)

Function 

Prevents polymer degradation when exposed to sunlight. UV stabilizers include two main groups: 
  • UV Absorbers – absorb and convert UV energy. 
  • HALS (Hindered Amine Light Stabilizers) – neutralize free radicals and help the polymer “self-heal.” 

Benefits 

  • Reduces cracking and surface chalking. 
  • Maintains color stability and minimizes deformation. 
  • Increases outdoor durability for 3–10 years depending on grade. 

Applications 

  • Greenhouse films, agricultural films. 
  • Outdoor products: plastic chairs, flower pots, pallets, waste bins. 
  • Water pipes exposed to sunlight. 
 
  1. Slip & Anti-block Additives

Slip Agents 

  • Reduce coefficient of friction (COF) between film layers. 
  • Ensure smooth winding and packaging without sticking. 

Anti-block Agents 

  • Prevent film layers from sticking together during storage and processing. 
  • Improve efficiency in high-speed film production. 

Applications 

  • PE, PP films. 
  • Food and industrial packaging. 
  • Shopping bags, freezer bags, general packaging films. 
 
  1. Anti-static Additives

Function 

Create a conductive surface layer to dissipate static charges. 

Benefits 

  • Prevents dust attraction. 
  • Reduces static “crackling” noises. 
  • Ensures safety when packaging electronic components. 

Applications 

  • Anti-dust PE/PP films. 
  • Electronic packaging. 
  • Injection molded products requiring clean surfaces. 
 
  1. Processing Aids (PPA)

Function 

Enhance polymer flow behavior during extrusion or film blowing. 

Benefits 

  • Reduces die build-up and improves film gloss. 
  • Increases output and lowers energy consumption. 
  • Prevents melt fracture and sagging during film blowing. 

Applications 

  • PE, PP blown film. 
  • Pipe extrusion. 
  • HDPE blow molding. 
 
  1. Fillers
Common fillers include CaCO₃, talc, and barium sulfate. 

Benefits 

  • Reduces material cost. 
  • Improves stiffness, whiteness, or opacity. 
  • Enhances dimensional stability and reduces shrinkage. 

Applications 

  • PP raffia and woven bags. 
  • PE/PP films. 
  • Pipes, sheets, industrial parts. 
 
  1. Color Masterbatch

Function 

Provides color based on Pantone or RAL standards for plastic products. 

Benefits 

  • Excellent color dispersion. 
  • High thermal stability and strong colorfastness. 
  • Dust-free and safe for production environments. 

Applications 

  • Packaging. 
  • Household goods, toys. 
  • Injection molded products. 
 
  1. Flame Retardants

Function 

Slow down or prevent polymers from catching fire, essential for electrical and electronic components. 

Benefits 

  • Reduces flame spread. 
  • Lowers smoke emission. 
  • Meets UL94 safety requirements. 

Applications 

  • Electrical housings. 
  • Automotive and electronic components. 
  • Building materials. 
 
  1. Impact Modifiers
Common types: CPE, ABS, EVA, MBS. 

Benefits 

  • Improve toughness and flexibility. 
  • Prevent cracking under impact or low temperatures. 
  • Ideal for products requiring high mechanical strength. 

Applications 

  • Outdoor PVC pipes. 
  • Thick-walled injection molded parts. 
  • Food packaging. 
 
  1. Lubricants

Function 

Reduce friction between polymer–metal surfaces and polymer–polymer interactions. 

Benefits 

  • Lower energy consumption. 
  • Improve mold release. 
  • Enhance production efficiency. 

Applications 

  • Injection molding. 
  • Extrusion and film blowing. 
  • Rigid and flexible PVC products. 
 

Conclusion 

Plastic additives are indispensable in modern plastic production. Each type offers unique benefits: improved mechanical performance, thermal stability, outdoor durability, process optimization, and reduced material cost. Choosing the right additives enables manufacturers to produce high-quality, consistent, and competitive products.

item.title: What Are PP Reprocessed Granules and Their Applications?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
As global manufacturing increasingly shifts toward cost-effective and sustainable material solutions, PP reprocessed granules — also known as recycled PP granules — have become a strategic choice for many industries. These granules offer a balance of performance, affordability and environmental benefits, making them a preferred option for packaging, injection molding, automotive parts, household goods, and more. 
  1. What Are PP Reprocessed Granules?
PP reprocessed granules are polypropylene pellets produced by recycling post-industrial or post-consumer PP waste. The recycled material is collected, cleaned, melted, and re-extruded into uniform granules that can be used in a wide range of manufacturing processes.  Depending on the input material and processing quality, PP reprocessed granules can be categorized into: 
  • Grade A (near-virgin quality): High strength, consistent color, suitable for higher-spec applications. 
  • Grade B–C: More cost-effective, used for products with lower mechanical requirements. 
Common colors include black, grey, natural and off-white, depending on the source and filtration process.     
  1. Key Properties of PP Reprocessed Granules
Even though they are recycled, PP reprocessed granules retain many of the desirable characteristics that make PP one of the world’s most widely used plastics. 

2.1. Good Mechanical Strength 

Reprocessed PP is known for its toughness and impact resistance, making it suitable for durable items such as crates, storage boxes, and household products. 

2.2. Chemical and Heat Resistance 

PP remains stable when exposed to acids, alkalis, and detergents, and can withstand temperatures between 100°C and 130°C, depending on the grade. 

2.3. Lightweight and Easy to Process 

Manufacturers appreciate PP for its low density, which helps reduce product weight and shipping costs. Reprocessed PP also performs well in: 
  • Injection molding 
  • Extrusion 
  • Blow molding 
  • Fiber and yarn production 

2.4. Cost-Effective 

Compared to virgin PP, reprocessed granules can reduce raw material costs by 20–50%, depending on specification. 

2.5. Eco-Friendly 

Using recycled PP supports sustainability goals, minimizes plastic waste, and helps companies meet global environmental standards.   
  1. How PP Reprocessed Granules Are Produced
The production process involves several steps to ensure clean, uniform, and stable-quality granules: 
  1. Collection of PP Waste: From manufacturing scraps, rejected products, or post-consumer sources. 
  1. Sorting: Removing contaminants and separating PP from other plastics. 
  1. Washing and Drying: Eliminating dust, labels, oil residue, or adhesives. 
  1. Shredding: Cutting PP waste into small flakes. 
  1. Extrusion and Melting: The flakes are melted and filtered to remove any remaining impurities. 
  1. Pelletizing: The melted PP is cut into uniform granules and cooled. 
  1. Quality Control and Packaging: Granules are inspected for color, melt flow index (MFI), strength, and stability. 
Advanced recycling lines produce higher-purity granules suitable for more demanding applications.   
  1. Applications of PP Reprocessed Granules
Thanks to their versatility and cost savings, PP reprocessed granules are used across numerous industries. 

4.1. Packaging and PP Woven Bags 

High-quality recycled PP is widely used for: 
  • Woven sacks 
  • PP fabric 
  • FIBC bags (big bags) 
  • Agricultural and fertilizer packaging 
  • Ropes and twine 
These products do not require virgin-grade PP, making recycled PP a perfect fit. 

4.2. Household Products 

Manufacturers use PP reprocessed granules to produce: 
  • Buckets, basins, and dustbins 
  • Hangers 
  • Storage boxes 
  • Baskets and trays 
  • Low-pressure pipes 
The material offers good durability without inflating production cost. 

4.3. Automotive Components 

Recycled PP is used in non-critical plastic parts such as: 
  • Inner panels 
  • Mudguards 
  • Storage compartments 
  • Battery casings 
Its toughness and dimensional stability make it a dependable choice. 

4.4. Electrical and Electronic Accessories 

Parts that do not require virgin specifications — like covers, housings, and protective casings — can be made using high-grade recycled PP. 

4.5. Construction and Industrial Uses 

The construction industry relies on PP reprocessed granules for: 
  • Floor protection sheets 
  • Cable conduits 
  • Drainage components 
  • Accessories and fittings 
They offer good strength and are a more economical substitute for virgin PP.   
  1. Why Manufacturers Choose PP Reprocessed Granules

✔ Major Cost Savings 

Raw material cost drops significantly, improving overall profitability, especially for high-volume production. 

✔ Easy to Customize 

Manufacturers can blend recycled PP with virgin PP or add fillers and additives to enhance: 
  • Strength 
  • Flexibility 
  • Heat resistance 
  • Color consistency 

✔ Large and Stable Supply 

PP waste is abundant globally, making reprocessed PP a reliable long-term material source. 

✔ Supports Sustainability Goals 

Using recycled PP helps companies comply with international environmental policies and aligns with global sustainability trends.   
  1. Should You Use PP Reprocessed Granules?
If your product does not require strict virgin-grade performance, PP reprocessed granules are an excellent choice. They offer: 
  • Competitive pricing 
  • Sufficient mechanical strength 
  • Versatility in processing 
  • Consistent availability 
  • Environmental benefits 
Industries like packaging, household goods, agricultural supplies, and general injection molding can benefit greatly from switching to recycled PP.     

Conclusion 

PP reprocessed granules are a practical, economical, and sustainable material solution for modern manufacturing. With strong mechanical properties, diverse applications, and substantial cost advantages, they continue to gain popularity in global markets.  Companies that adopt recycled PP not only reduce production costs, but also contribute to environmental protection and circular economy principles.

item.title: Antioxidant for Plastics: Definition, Benefits, and Applications in the Plastics Industry
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
[Mascom Global] During the production and use of plastic products, materials are continuously exposed to heat, oxygen, light, and mechanical stress. These factors trigger oxidation, a chemical reaction that breaks polymer chains and causes plastics to degrade over time. To prevent this, antioxidant for plastics is added as a crucial additive to stabilize the material and extend product lifespan.

1. What Is Antioxidant for Plastics?

Antioxidants for plastics are additives incorporated into polymers to prevent or slow down oxidation that occurs during: 
  • Plastic processing (extrusion, injection molding, blow molding…) 
  • Storage of raw materials 
  • End-use under environmental exposure 
When polymers undergo oxidation, their molecular chains break down, leading to: 
  • Brittleness and cracking 
  • Yellowing or discoloration 
  • Loss of tensile strength and elasticity 
  • Reduced mechanical properties 
  • Rapid aging and degradation 
Antioxidants work by scavenging free radicals or decomposing hydroperoxides before they attack polymer chains. This keeps the polymer structure stable for a longer period. 

2. Types of Antioxidants Used in Plastics

In practice, antioxidants are divided into two main categories: 

2.1. Primary Antioxidants 

Primary antioxidants mainly function as free-radical scavengers, especially under heat during processing.  Common types include: 
  • Phenolic antioxidants (hindered phenols such as BHT, Irganox 1010, Irganox 1076) 
  • Aminic antioxidants (less common in white plastics because they may cause discoloration) 
Main function: Improve thermal stability during processing, reduce gel formation, prevent burn marks, and minimize discoloration. 

2.2. Secondary Antioxidants 

Secondary antioxidants primarily decompose hydroperoxides, which otherwise cause polymer breakdown when exposed to oxygen.  Common types include: 
  • Phosphite antioxidants (e.g., Irgafos 168) 
  • Thioesters 
Main function: Long-term stabilization under environmental exposure. 

2.3. Combination Systems (Primary + Secondary) 

Most modern applications use a combination of primary and secondary antioxidants for the best performance. One of the most widely used systems is: 
  • AO 1010 + AO 168 → Provides dual protection and excellent heat stability. 
This combination is commonly used in: 
  • Compounds 
  • Color and white masterbatch 
  • Filler masterbatch 
  • Recycled plastic materials 

3. Benefits of Using Antioxidants in Plastics

3.1. Prevent Aging and Extend Product Lifespan 

Antioxidants protect the polymer from: 
  • Heat 
  • Oxygen 
  • UV exposure (when used together with UV stabilizers) 
  • Oxidation during use 
This prevents brittleness, cracking, and surface deterioration. 

3.2. Maintain Color Stability and Prevent Yellowing 

Oxidized plastics, especially PP, PE, and EVA, tend to discolor. Antioxidants help: 
  • Maintain bright, clean color 
  • Stabilize color tone 
  • Minimize yellowing at high processing temperatures 

3.3. Improve Mechanical Properties 

By preventing chain scission, the polymer retains its: 
  • Tensile strength 
  • Elongation 
  • Impact strength 
  • Stiffness 
  • Load-bearing performance 
This is especially important for blown film, T-shirt bags, shrink film, raffia, and plastic pipes. 

3.4. Enhance Processing Stability 

Antioxidants reduce: 
  • Gel formation and black spots 
  • Burn marks 
  • Smoke and odor during extrusion 
  • Filter clogging 
  • Polymer degradation in the extruder 
This provides significant efficiency benefits: fewer defects, higher output, and lower production costs. 

4. Applications of Antioxidants in the Plastics Industry

Antioxidants are widely used in almost all major polymer types. 

4.1. Films (Blown Film, T-shirt Bags, LDPE/HDPE Film) 

They help: 
  • Prevent film burning 
  • Maintain tensile strength and elongation 
  • Increase outdoor durability 
  • Preserve whiteness and gloss 

4.2. Raffia and Woven Sack Production 

Used to: 
  • Maintain fiber strength 
  • Prevent filament breakage at high speeds 
  • Ensure stability during stretching 

4.3. Injection and Blow Molding 

Common applications include: 
  • Plastic containers 
  • Household goods 
  • Bottles 
  • Hollow packaging 
Antioxidants prevent brittleness and cracking over time. 

4.4. Compounding, Masterbatch, and Filler 

Antioxidants are essential in masterbatch and filler production to: 
  • Stabilize the polymer during high-temperature processing 
  • Improve pigment dispersion 
  • Reduce burn marks and black spots 
  • Extend shelf life of materials 

4.5. Recycled Plastics 

Recycled polymers often arrive already partially oxidized. Adding antioxidants helps: 
  • Improve strength and durability 
  • Reduce burnt smell 
  • Prevent further color degradation 
  • Enhance melt flow and processing behavior 

5. How to Choose the Right Antioxidant

Depending on the application, manufacturers may select: 
  • AO 1010 → Long-term oxidation resistance 
  • AO 168 → Processing protection against heat 
  • AO 1010 + AO 168 → Most common and cost-effective solution 
  • Phosphite antioxidants → Suitable for high-temperature applications 
  • Specialty AO systems → For engineering plastics (PA, PC, ABS) 
Key considerations: 
  • Processing temperature 
  • Final product color (white plastics require non-discoloring AO) 
  • Dosage level 
  • Amount of recycled material used 

6. Conclusion

Antioxidants for plastics play a vital role in: 
  • Polymer stabilization 
  • Preventing thermal and oxidative degradation 
  • Preserving mechanical properties 
  • Maintaining color 
  • Reducing processing defects 
  • Extending product life 
Although used at low concentrations (0.1–0.5%), antioxidants have a major impact on the overall performance and durability of plastic products.

Polyethylene bags (PE bags) are among the most widely used plastic packaging products globally. They appear in supermarkets, food packaging, industrial wrapping, healthcare, and everyday consumer goods. To produce a PE bag that meets strict standards for strength, clarity, durability and load capacity, manufacturers must follow a precise, highly controlled production process—from raw material selection to film blowing, printing, cutting, and sealing. 
  1. What Is a PE Bag? — Quick Overview
PE bags are made from polyethylene, primarily categorized into: 
  • HDPE – high rigidity, matte surface 
  • LDPE – soft, flexible, glossy; often used for supermarket and food bags 
  • LLDPE – strongest tensile strength and stretchability; commonly blended with HDPE/LDPE for better film quality 
Thanks to their flexibility, durability, and cost efficiency, PE bags make up over 70% of the global flexible packaging market.   
  1. Standard PE Bag Manufacturing Process
A complete nylon bag production line includes five key stages: 
  1. Raw Material Preparation 
  1. PE Film Blowing 
  1. Printing (if required) 
  1. Bag Cutting & Sealing 
  1. Packaging & Storage 
Let’s examine each step.   

2.1 Raw Material Preparation — The Foundation of Film Quality 

This is the most decisive step, directly affecting film strength, transparency, and stability.  Common materials include: 
  • Virgin PE resins (HDPE, LDPE, LLDPE) 
  • Color Masterbatch – for custom colors and branding 
  • Filler Masterbatch – to optimize cost, enhance stiffness, improve film stability 
  • Additives Masterbatch – UV protection, slip additives, anti-block, lubricants, desiccant masterbatch, etc. 
At this stage, Mascom’s masterbatch solutions help manufacturers achieve: 
  • Excellent dispersibility 
  • Consistent pellet quality 
  • Lower moisture content → reduce defects 
  • Improved mechanical properties and film stability 
  All materials must be mixed uniformly using an industrial mixer to ensure even dispersion and stable melt flow.  Moisture must be completely eliminated—otherwise, defects will occur: 
  • Fish eyes 
  • Pinholes, air bubbles 
  • Weak film strength 
  • Hazy, low-gloss surface 
  • Uneven thickness 
 

2.2 PE Film Blowing — The Heart of the Entire Process 

Film blowing is the most critical stage, where raw material is transformed into PE film.  Process steps: 
  1. Material is fed into the extruder 
  1. Melted polymer exits the die as a tubular bubble 
  1. Air inflates the bubble 
  1. The bubble is cooled 
  1. Film is flattened and wound into rolls 
  Key parameters to control: 
  • Barrel zone temperatures 
  • Blow-up ratio 
  • Film take-off speed 
  • Film thickness 
  • Clarity, gloss, tensile strength 
  • Material blending ratios 
Common defects in film blowing: 
  • Streaks / flow lines 
  • Fish eyes 
  • Wrinkles from unstable pressure 
  • Film tearing 
  • Thickness inconsistency 
Using Mascom Filler Masterbatch and Additives Masterbatch ensures: 
  • Smooth film processing 
  • Reduced die build-up 
  • Better opacity or stiffness when required 
  • Stable extrusion and fewer defects 
Up to 80% of final bag quality depends on this stage.   

2.3 Printing — Adding Brand Identity to PE Bags 

Supermarket bags, food bags, garbage bags, and retail packaging often require Flexo or Rotogravure printing.  Key factors to control: 
  • Ink adhesion 
  • No smearing or blurring 
  • Proper machine speed 
  • No streaks or ink lift 
  • Color consistency across rolls 
Mascom Color Masterbatch ensures highly stable color tone, heat resistance, and excellent dispersion—helping printers achieve vibrant and consistent branding.   

2.4 Bag Cutting & Sealing — The Step Closest to the End User 

From printed or non-printed rolls, bag-making machines produce various PE bag types:  Common PE bags include: 
  • T-shirt bags 
  • Garbage bags 
  • Bottom-seal bags 
  • Flat bags 
  • Zipper bags 
  • Biodegradable bags (when using bio-resin) 
Key parameters: 
  • Sealing temperature 
  • Machine speed 
  • Bag dimensions 
  • Seal strength 
Common defects: 
  • Weak sealing / bottom bursting 
  • Incomplete cutting 
  • Misalignment 
  • Burned edges 
Seal quality directly affects the customer’s experience with the product.   

2.5 Packaging & Storage — Protecting Film Quality 

After bag cutting: 
  • Bags are counted 
  • Packed in bundles or rolls 
  • Wrapped in PE/PP or placed in cartons 
  • Stored away from sunlight to prevent oxidation 
This maintains durability during transport and long-term storage.   
  1. Why Optimizing the PE Bag Production Process Matters
A well-controlled manufacturing system leads to: 

✔ Reduced raw material waste 

Better film stability → less scrap. 

✔ Stronger bags & fewer complaints 

Uniform film and strong sealing. 

✔ Higher productivity 

Stable machines → faster cycles. 

✔ Better brand reputation 

High-quality PE bags represent professionalism.  Mascom masterbatch products—including Filler Masterbatch, Color Masterbatch, and Additives Masterbatch—help factories achieve higher consistency, reduced defects and improved mechanical performance, ultimately boosting competitiveness in the global packaging market.   
  1. Conclusion
Producing PE bags involves five interconnected steps: raw material preparation, film blowing, printing, cutting & sealing, and packaging. Each stage requires precise technical control to ensure top-quality final products. By understanding and optimizing every phase—combined with high-performance masterbatch solutions from Mascom Global—manufacturers can reduce defects, increase efficiency, and strengthen their position in the fast-growing plastic packaging industry.

In the modern landscape of polymer materials, the boundary between plastic and metal is becoming increasingly blurred. Engineering Plastics are rapidly replacing traditional materials like brass, steel, and glass, offering superior weight-to-strength ratios and innovative design flexibility. Among the elite tier of high-performance thermoplastics, Polysulfone (PSU) stands out as a material of choice for the most demanding applications.  But what exactly is Polysulfone? Why has it become the gold standard for industries ranging from aerospace to medical healthcare? And, crucially, how can manufacturers overcome the technical challenges associated with processing this high-temperature material?  In this deep dive, we explore the chemistry, capabilities, and industrial applications of PSU, while highlighting how Mascom Global supports the industry with advanced additive and compound solutions. 
  1. DefiningPolysulfone(PSU) 
Polysulfone (PSU) is a rigid, high-strength, semi-transparent thermoplastic belonging to the sulfone polymer family. Chemically, it is an amorphous polymer defined by its repeating sulfone groups and aryl groups within its molecular chain.  This unique molecular architecture provides PSU with exceptional stability—both thermal and chemical. Unlike commodity plastics that may soften or degrade under stress, PSU maintains its structural integrity. 
  • Appearance: Naturally, PSU possesses a distinct transparent amber color, though it can be colored to meet specific aesthetic requirements. 
  • Thermal Profile: With a high Glass Transition Temperature of approximately 185°C, PSU is categorized as a high-heat plastic, capable of maintaining rigorous physical properties across a wide temperature range. 
  1. Key Technical Properties: Why Choose PSU?
To understand why engineers specify PSU for critical components, we must look at its core technical characteristics. It offers a balance of properties that few other thermoplastics can match. 

Excellent Heat Resistance and Thermal Stability 

PSU is designed for endurance. It boasts a continuous service temperature of 150°C to 160°C. More impressively, it exhibits outstanding resistance to thermal oxidation. While many plastics become brittle or discolored after prolonged exposure to heat, PSU retains its mechanical strength and transparency, making it ideal for electrical and automotive components. 

Superior Hydrolytic Stability 

Perhaps the most defining feature of Polysulfone is its Hydrolytic Stability. PSU is virtually unaffected by hydrolysis. It can withstand prolonged exposure to hot water and rigorous steam sterilization cycles (autoclaving) without chemical degradation or cracking. This specific property makes it a superior alternative to polycarbonate (PC) in medical environments where repeated sterilization is mandatory. 

Chemical Resistance and Dimensional Stability 

  • Chemical Resistance: PSU offers high resistance to mineral acids, alkali solutions, saline environments, and oils/greases (though it is sensitive to polar solvents like ketones). 
  • Dimensional Precision: Due to its amorphous structure, PSU exhibits low mold shrinkage and excellent creep resistance. Parts molded from PSU hold tight tolerances over long periods, preventing the "warpage" issues common in semi-crystalline plastics. 

Outstanding Dielectric Properties 

Even at elevated temperatures or in humid environments, PSU acts as an excellent electrical insulator, making it indispensable for connectors, coil bobbins, and circuit board substrates. 
  1. Breakthrough Applications in Modern Industry
Leveraging these superior properties, Polysulfone has found its way into critical "failure-is-not-an-option" applications: 

Medical and Healthcare 

In an industry where hygiene and safety are paramount, PSU is a top-tier material. Its ability to withstand repeated autoclaving allows it to be used in: 
  • Reusable surgical instruments and handles. 
  • Hemodialysis membrane holders and respiratory devices. 
  • Medical instrument trays and dental equipment. 

Water Treatment and Membrane Technology 

PSU serves as the foundational material for manufacturing membranes used in Reverse Osmosis (RO) and Ultrafiltration (UF) systems. Its ability to control pore size combined with chemical durability ensures these membranes function reliably in harsh filtration environments. Additionally, it is used in plumbing fittings (replacing brass) to prevent heavy metal leaching. 

Food and Beverage Contact 

Meeting strict safety standards (such as FDA regulations), PSU is widely utilized in: 
  • Internal components of high-end coffee machines (valves, boilers). 
  • Milking machine components. 
  • Microwavable cookware and food containers. 

Automotive and Aerospace 

In sectors driven by fuel efficiency, weight reduction is key. PSU’s natural flame retardancy (self-extinguishing) and lightweight nature make it perfect for: 
  • Aircraft interior panels and lighting bezels. 
  • Under-the-hood automotive sensors. 
  • Electrical connectors exposed to engine heat. 
  1. The Processing Challenge: Where Expertise Matters
While Polysulfone is a "super material," it is notoriously difficult to process.  High melting temperatures and high melt viscosity pose significant challenges during Injection Molding or Extrusion. Manufacturers often face issues such as: 
  • Unstable Melt Flow Index (MFI): Leading to inconsistent product quality. 
  • Poor Dispersion: Standard colorants or additives often degrade or disperse poorly at PSU processing temperatures, causing streaks or specks. 
  • Surface Defects: Flow marks and warpage can occur if the material formulation isn't optimized. 
To unlock the full potential of PSU and reduce scrap rates, manufacturers often require Specialized Additive Masterbatches or Custom Compounds. These solutions are designed to improve flow, enhance surface finish, or provide stable coloration without compromising the polymer’s heat resistance. 
  1. MascomGlobal: Your Strategic Partner for Material Solutions 
In the competitive world of engineering plastics, selecting the right raw material partner is as critical as selecting the resin itself. This is where Mascom Global JSC steps in.  As a leading manufacturer of Masterbatch and Compound in Vietnam, Mascom Global does not just sell products; we provide "Real Value Commitment" to polymer manufacturers worldwide. We understand the intricacies of processing high-performance plastics and offer solutions that bridge the gap between technical difficulty and commercial viability. 

Why Partner with Mascom Global? 

  • Massive Manufacturing Scale: 
Operating a state-of-the-art facility in the Tien Tien Industrial Cluster, Mascom Global utilizes over 50 advanced production lines with a total capacity of 240,000 tons/year. This scale ensures we can meet the volume demands of major international buyers. 
  • Comprehensive Product Ecosystem: 
Our R&D center has developed over 100 high-quality product codes. Beyond our famous Filler Masterbatch, we specialize in: 
  • Color Masterbatches: Offering excellent dispersion and thermal stability, suitable for various resin carriers. 
  • Additive Masterbatches: Solutions like Processing Aids (PPA) to improve flow in viscous materials or Anti-oxidants to protect polymers during high-heat processing. 
  • Engineering Compounds: Tailored formulations to meet specific technical requirements. 
  • International Quality Standards: 
Quality is our baseline. Our factory is ISO 9001:2015 certified. Furthermore, our products comply with rigorous global safety standards, including FDA approved, REACH, and ROHS compliance, ensuring they are safe for use in sensitive applications like food packaging and medical devices. 
  • Global Reach: 
We have successfully exported to over 70 countries across Europe, Africa, South America, and Asia. Our experience in diverse markets allows us to understand local requirements and logistics, making us a reliable link in your global supply chain. 
  1. Conclusion
Polysulfone (PSU) is set to remain a cornerstone of material innovation, driving advancements in healthcare, automotive, and purification technologies thanks to its unbeatable thermal and hydrolytic stability. However, working with such advanced materials requires expertise.  To maximize your production efficiency and product quality, you need a partner who understands polymer science. Whether you need a stable Color Masterbatch that withstands high heat, or a cost-effective Compound solution, Mascom Global is ready to serve.  Ready to optimize your plastic production?  Contact the experts at Mascom Global today. We don't just supply materials; we deliver the technical solutions that keep you ahead of the competition.

In the rapidly evolving world of logistics and packaging, Polypropylene (PP) Corrugated Sheets — often known by trade names like Danpla, Coroplast, or Twin-wall sheets — have emerged as the ultimate replacement for traditional cardboard. However, the secret to producing high-quality, durable, and cost-effective sheets lies not just in the resin, but in the advanced Additive Masterbatch solutions used during extrusion.
  1. What are Polypropylene Corrugated Sheets?
Polypropylene Corrugated Sheets are extruded twin-wall plastic sheets consisting of two flat surfaces connected by vertical ribs (flutes). Made primarily from Polypropylene Impact Copolymer, these sheets offer a unique combination of durability and lightweight properties. Key Technical Advantages:
  • High Strength-to-Weight Ratio: The I-beam structure provides excellent rigidity while remaining lighter than wood or solid PVC.
  • Chemical & Water Resistance: Unlike cardboard, PP sheets are chemically inert (hydrophobic), making them waterproof and resistant to acids and oils.
  • Recyclability: They are 100% recyclable, aligning with circular economy trends.
 
  1. Applications of Additives: Optimizing PP Corrugated Sheet Production
Producing a flawless PP sheet requires overcoming complex rheological challenges in the extruder. This is where Mascom Global’s Masterbatch solutions become indispensable. 2.1 Filler Masterbatch (CaCO3): The Backbone of Efficiency While often viewed merely as a cost-reduction tool, high-quality Filler Masterbatch (Calcium Carbonate) plays a crucial technical role in sheet extrusion.
  • Increased Productivity: CaCO3 has higher thermal conductivity than PP resin. Adding Mascom’s Filler Masterbatch allows the sheet to cool faster in the calibration unit, enabling higher line speeds and shorter cycle times.
  • Dimensional Stability: Fillers increase the stiffness (modulus) of the sheet and reduce shrinkage, preventing warpage during cooling.
2.2 Processing Aid Masterbatch (PPA): Eliminating Surface Defects In thin-wall extrusion, friction between the viscous PP melt and the metal die can cause melt fracture (sharkskin effect) or die lines.
  • Solution: Mascom’s PPA Masterbatch (MC-PPA01) creates a microscopic lubricating layer on the die wall. This eliminates melt fracture, reduces die build-up, and lowers extrusion pressure/energy consumption.
2.3 Anti-UV Masterbatch: Extending Outdoor Lifespan PP is naturally susceptible to UV degradation, leading to chalking and cracking within months of outdoor exposure (e.g., agricultural tree guards or signage).
  • Solution: Using Anti-UV Masterbatch containing Hindered Amine Light Stabilizers (HALS) neutralizes free radicals generated by UV radiation. This allows PP corrugated sheets to maintain mechanical strength and color for 2-5 years outdoors.
2.4 Anti-static Masterbatch: Protecting Electronics For ESD (Electrostatic Discharge) packaging boxes used in the electronics industry, standard PP acts as an insulator that can build up dangerous static charges.
  • Solution: Anti-static Masterbatch (MC-AST01) migrates to the sheet surface, absorbing atmospheric moisture to form a conductive layer. This dissipates static charges, protecting sensitive circuit boards from damage and preventing dust attraction.
  1. Why Choose Mascom Global for Your Masterbatch Needs?
As a leading manufacturer based in Vietnam, Mascom Global understands that every extrusion line is unique. We don't just sell additives; we provide tailored technical solutions.
  • Consistent Quality: Certified by ISO 9001:2015, ensuring stable MFI and dispersion in every batch.
  • Wide Range of Products: From high-load CaCO3 Filler to specialized additives like Color, UV, Slip, and Anti-block.
  • Global Reach: Exporting to over 70 countries, we meet the stringent standards of the European, US, and Asian markets.
  Conclusion Kết Luận Polypropylene corrugated sheets are revolutionizing sustainable packaging, but their performance relies heavily on the correct additive strategy. Whether you need to increase stiffness with Filler Masterbatch, ensure outdoor durability with Anti-UV, or improve surface finish with Processing Aids, Mascom Global has the expertise to optimize your production.

item.title: Composite Pipe & Leading Manufacturers
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
[Mascom Global] In recent years, demand for composite pipe systems has increased significantly across industries such as construction, oil and gas, water supply, and infrastructure development. Traditional materials like metal and conventional plastics are gradually being replaced or supplemented by more advanced solutions that offer higher durability, corrosion resistance, and long-term performance. One of the most notable innovations in this field is the development of multi-layer piping technology. These products have gained widespread recognition due to their ability to combine the advantages of multiple materials into a single structure. This article provides a comprehensive overview of what composite pipes are, their key characteristics, and an introduction to some of the leading manufacturers in the global market.  

What is a Composite Pipe? 

(Illustrative purpose only)

The pipe is a type of pipe made from two or more different materials combined together to achieve superior performance compared to traditional single-material pipes. These materials typically include layers of plastic (such as PE or PP), metal (such as aluminum), or reinforcing fibers.  The most common structure includes: 
  • An inner layer made of polyethylene (PE) or polypropylene (PP)  
  • A middle layer reinforced with aluminum or fiber  
  • An outer protective layer made of polymer  
This multi-layer construction allows these pipes to deliver a combination of mechanical strength, flexibility, chemical resistance, and thermal stability. 

Key Advantages of Composite Pipes 

High Strength and Durability 

These products are designed to withstand high pressure and mechanical stress. The reinforcement layer, whether aluminum or fiber-based, significantly improves the pipe’s structural integrity, making it suitable for demanding applications. 

Corrosion Resistance 

Unlike metal pipes, composite pipes do not corrode when exposed to water, chemicals, or environmental factors. This makes them ideal for long-term use in water supply systems, chemical transport, and industrial applications.  

Lightweight and Easy Installation 

Compared to traditional steel pipes, composite pipes are much lighter, which simplifies  transportation and installation. This reduces labor costs and installation time, especially in large-scale projects.  

Thermal and Chemical Stability 

The pipes can maintain stable performance under varying temperatures and chemical exposure. This is particularly important in applications such as hot water systems, oil and gas pipelines, and industrial fluid transport. 

Long Service Life 

Due to their resistance to corrosion, wear, and environmental degradation, these products offer a longer service life compared to conventional materials. This reduces maintenance costs and ensures reliable operation over time. 

Applications of Composite Pipes 

(Illustrative purpose only)

These type of pipes are widely used across multiple industries due to their versatility and performance advantages. 

Water Supply and Plumbing Systems 

Composite pipes are commonly used in residential and commercial plumbing systems. Their corrosion resistance and durability make them ideal for both cold and hot water distribution. 

Oil and Gas Industry 

In the oil and gas sector, these pipes are used for transporting fluids under highpressure and harsh conditions. Their resistance to corrosion and chemicals makes them a reliable alternative to metal pipes.  

Agriculture and Irrigation 

Composite pipes are also used in irrigation systems due to their lightweight nature and resistance to environmental factors. They help improve efficiency and reduce  maintenance in agricultural operations. 

Industrial Applications 

Many industries use these products for transporting chemicals, gases, and other materials. Their chemical resistance and durability make them suitable for demanding environments. 

Construction and Infrastructure 

Composite pipes are increasingly used in modern construction projects, including heating systems, drainage systems, and structural applications.  

Leading Manufacturers 

The global composite pipe market is highly competitive, with several well-established manufacturers known for their advanced technology, large-scale production capacity, and consistent product quality. 

Advanced Drainage Systems (ADS) – USA 

ADS is one of the leading manufacturers of water management and drainage solutions. The company produces a wide range of composite piping systems designed for infrastucture and environmental applications. With extensive manufacturing facilities and strong R&D capabilities, ADS serves both domestic and international markets. 

Aliaxis Group – Belgium 

Aliaxis is a global leader in advanced piping systems, including composite pipes. The company operates in more than 40 countries and offers innovative solutions for water, gas, and industrial applications. Its strong focus on sustainability and innovation makes it a key player in the industry.  

Georg Fischer (GF Piping Systems) – Switzerland 

GF Piping Systems is known for its high-performance piping solutions, including composite materials. The company specializes in industrial, utility, and building technology applications. Its products are widely recognized for precision, reliability, and long-term performance. 

Pipelife International – Austria 

Pipelife is one of Europe’s largest manufacturers of plastic and composite piping systems. With a strong presence in multiple regions, the company provides solutions for infrastructure, agriculture, and construction projects. 

Sekisui Chemical – Japan 

Sekisui Chemical is a leading Japanese manufacturer specializing in advanced materials and piping systems. The company has developed high quality composite pipes used in water supply, industrial, and infrastructure applications. 

China Lesso Group – China 

China Lesso is one of the largest plastic piping manufacturers in Asia. The company offers a wide range of composite pipe products and has a strong production capacity supported by multiple manufacturing bases. 

Conclusion 

Composite pipes represent a significant advancement in piping technology, combining the strengths of multiple materials to deliver superior performance. With advantages such as high durability, corrosion resistance, lightweight design, and long service life, they are becoming the preferred choice across many industries.  As global demand for efficient and sustainable infrastructure continues to grow, composite pipes will play an increasingly important role in shaping the future of piping systems.Choosing high-quality products from reliable manufacturers is essential to ensure long-term performance and cost efficiency.

item.title: What is Wood Plastic Composite (WPC)?
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
[Mascom Global] In the evolving world of sustainable construction and interior design, Wood Plastic Composite (WPC) has emerged as a revolutionary material. By blending the natural aesthetic of wood with the durability of modern polymers, WPC offers a versatile solution that addresses the limitations of traditional timber. This article explores the composition, manufacturing process, advantages, and diverse applications of this innovative hybrid material. 

Understanding Wood Plastic Composite 

(Illustrative purpose only)

Wood Plastic Composite is a hybrid material composed of natural wood fibers (or wood flour) and thermoplastic resins, such as Polyethylene (PE), Polypropylene (PP), or Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC). Typically, the mixture consists of about 50% to 70% wood cellulose and 30% to 50% plastic polymer.  Beyond the primary components, specialized additives like coupling agents, UV stabilizers, pigments, and lubricants are incorporated during the manufacturing process. These additives ensure a homogenous bond between the organic wood and the synthetic plastic, resulting in a material that possesses the best qualities of both worlds. 

The Manufacturing Process 

The production of Wood Plastic Composite primarily involves a process called extrusion. In this method, the wood fibers and plastic pellets are heated until they reach a molten state. The mixture is then forced through a specific die or mold to create the desired shape, such as decking boards, railing profiles, or wall panels. Advanced manufacturers also use injection molding for more complex architectural component. This process allows for high precision and the ability to create textures that mimic natual wood grain with remarkable accuracy. 

Key Advantages of Wood Plastic Composite 

The rapid growth of the WPC market is attributed to several technical and economic benefits: 
  • Exceptional Durability: Unlike natural wood, WPC is highly resistant to rot, decay, and marine borers. It does not absorb moisture easily, which prevents warping, cracking, or splintering, common issues found in outdoor wooden structures. 
  • Low Maintenance: One of the most significant selling points for WPC is that it requires virtually no maintenance. It does not need to be sanded, stained, painted, or sealed. A simple cleaning with soap and water is usually sufficient to keep it looking new for decades. 
  • Aesthetic Versatility: WPC can be manufactured in a wide variety of colors, textures, and finishes. It provides the warm, inviting look of natural timber while offering the design flexibility of plastic. 
  • Environmental Sustainability: WPC is considered an eco-friendly material. It often utilizes recycled wood waste from the timber industry and recycled plastics (such as milk jugs or detergent bottles). Furthermore, the material itself is 100% recyclable at the end of its life cycle. 
  • Pest Resistance: Because of its plastic content, WPC is naturally resistant to termites and other wood-boring insects, making it an ideal choice for tropical climates or ground-contact applications. 
  • Safety: WPC boards are designed to be slip resistant and, more importantly, they do not splinter. This makes them a safer choice for families with children or pets, especially around swimming pools and decks. 

Primary Applications of Wood Plastic Composite 

(Illustrative purpose only)

The unique properties of wood plastic composite make it suitable for various industries: 
  • Outdoor Decking and Flooring: This is the most popular application. WPC decks are prized for their longevity and resistance to harsh weather conditions. 
  • Wall Cladding and Siding: Used in modern architecture to provide a sleek, "wood-look" exterior that remains vibrant without fading. 
  • Fencing and Railing: WPC provides a sturdy and attractive alternative to traditional wooden or metal fences. 
  • Outdoor Furniture: Benches, picnic tables, and park installments often use WPC due to its ability to withstand constant exposure to the sun and rain. 
  • Interior Decoration: Increasingly used for indoor wall panels, ceiling decorations, and flooring in high-moisture areas like kitchens and bathrooms. 

Conclusion 

Wood Plastic Composite represents a perfect synergy between nature and technology. It provides a high-performance, sustainable alternative to natural timber, reducing the pressure on forest resources while offering superior longevity. For contractors,  architects, and homeowners alike, WPC is more than just a building material; it is a smart investment in a durable and beautiful future.

item.title: Manufacturing Plastic Bags: From Raw Materials to Finished Products
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
[Mascom Global] In the modern industrial era, manufacturing plastic bags have become an indispensable part of commodity circulation and daily life. However, few people understand that behind a thin bag lies a complex technical process and meticulous chemical calculations. This article will dive deep into the world of the manufacturing plastic bags industry to explore the types of materials and the operation of a modern factory today.

  1. Primary Raw Materials in Manufacturing Plastic Bags Production

(Illustrative purpose only)

Materials are the decisive factor in the durability, transparency, and load-bearing capacity of a bag. When manufacturing plastic bags products, thermoplastic beads are commonly used today.

Polyethylene (PE) Resin 

This is the most common material, including two main variants: 
  • HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene): Has a high molecular density, creating a stiff, less stretchable bag. It is commonly found in supermarket bags or food bags. When lightly crumpled, HDPE bags produce a characteristic crackling sound. 
  • LDPE (Low-Density Polyethylene): Has a lower molecular density, giving the bag high transparency, a smooth surface, and better elasticity. LDPE is often used for clothing bags, cosmetics, or premium packaging. 

Polypropylene (PP) Resin 

PP bags are stiffer than PE and have excellent resistance to gas and water vapor. They are commonly used in packaging dry foods or products that need to maintain a fixed shape. 

Essential Additives 

In manufacturing plastic bags production, specific substances are often added to optimize performance:
  • Masterbatch (Colorant): Helps create a variety of colors for the bags. 
  • UV Blocking Agents: Protect the goods inside from degradation caused by sunlight. 
  • Biodegradable Additives: Help plastic bags decompose in the environment after a certain period (usually corn starch or organic compounds). 
  • Anti-Static Additives: Used for electronic component packaging to prevent static discharge. 

  1. Detailed Manufacturing Plastic Bags Process

This manufacturing plastic bags operation is typically carried out through four main stages, requiring seamless coordination between machinery and temperature control systems. 

Stage 1: Preparation and Mixing 

Virgin plastic resins are mixed with color masterbatches and additives in a specific ratio. This ratio is carefully calculated based on the thickness and technical requirements of the order. Modern factories use automatic dosing systems to ensure 100% consistency across batches. 

Stage 2: Extrusion & Blown Film 

This is the most critical stage of manufacturing plastic bags operation, determining the basic shape and quality of the film: 
  • Melting: The plastic mixture is fed into a hopper and moved to the extruder. Here, the plastic is heated and melted at temperatures ranging from 180°C to 230°C. 
  • Extrusion: The molten plastic is forced through a circular die to form a thin plastic tube. 
  • Blowing: A stream of air is blown into the center of the tube, inflating it like a long balloon (called a "plastic bubble"). Adjusting the air volume determines the width and thickness (microns) of the plastic film. 
  • Cooling: A cooling ring blows cold air around the bubble to immediately solidify the plastic film. 

Stage 3: Winding 

After cooling, the plastic bubble passes through a series of rollers that flatten it into a double-layered film. It is then wound into large film rolls. At this step, if the bag requires printing, the film surface undergoes a Corona Treatment. This process uses high-voltage discharge to increase the surface tension, allowing printing ink to adhere firmly. 

Stage 4: Printing & Finishing (Cutting) 

  • Printing: The film rolls are moved to a printing machine (usually Flexographic or Rotogravure) to print logos and brand information. 
  • Bag Cutting and Sealing: An automatic machine measures the dimensions and cuts individual bags from the roll. Simultaneously, a heat-sealing bar seals the bottom of the bag. 
  • Handle Punching: For "T-shirt bags" (supermarket bags), a hydraulic press punches out the handles at the end of the line.

  1. Technical Factors Influencing Quality of Manufacturing Plastic Bags Process

(Illustrative purpose only)

To produce a standard-compliant product, the factory must strictly control the following parameters: 
  • Melting Temperature: If the temperature is too high, the plastic degrades and loses strength. If it is too low, the plastic does not melt completely, causing "fish eyes" (lumps) on the surface. 
  • Air Blow Speed: Determines the uniformity of thickness. Uneven thickness makes the bag prone to tearing at thin spots. 
  • Screw Pressure: Ensures that the plastic is pushed out continuously and stably. 

  1. Deep Dive: Machinery in the Production Line

To operate the above process, a modern factory needs synchronized machinery: 

Blown Film Machine (The Heart) 

  • The Screw: Responsible for mixing and pushing the plastic. High-quality screws ensure the molten mixture is air-bubble-free. 
  • The Die Head: Determines the bag's width range. Professional factories often have various die heads to serve different sizes, from small medicine bags to large industrial liners. 

Printing Technology 

  • Flexo Printing: Best for large orders with simple designs. It is cost-effective and fast. 
  • Rotogravure Printing: For high-end bags requiring sharp images and absolute color precision. This is the top choice for major food brands. 

  1. Quality Control Standards (QC)

A reputable manufacturer must apply rigorous testing: 
  • Tensile Strength Test: Measures the maximum force a bag can withstand before breaking. 
  • Seal Strength: Ensures the bottom seal does not burst under heavy loads. 
  • Food Grade Certification: For food packaging, raw materials must meet FDA or equivalent standards to ensure no toxic chemicals leach into the food.

  1. Sustainable Trends and Biodegradable Bags

In the context of climate change, the industry is shifting toward eco-friendly solutions: 
  • Recycled Plastic Bags (PCR): Utilizing Post-Consumer Recycled resin to reduce ocean waste. 
  • Compostable Bags: Using plant-based materials like PLA (Polylactic Acid). These bags can fully decompose into water, CO2, and biomass within 6-12 months in composting conditions. 

Conclusion

In summary, the manufacturing plastic bags process is a closed supply chain, from resin selection and additive blending to advanced extrusion and printing techniques. With technological advancements, plastic bags today are not just containers; they are powerful branding tools that are becoming increasingly eco-friendly through innovations in bio-materials.  If you are looking for efficient packaging solutions or want to build a modern manufacturing plastic bags production line, always prioritize energy-saving technologies and sustainable materials to protect a green future.

item.title: How to Use Different Types of Color Masterbatch in Various Applications
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Color masterbatch plays an essential role in today’s plastic manufacturing industry by helping manufacturers achieve consistent coloration, improve product value and enhance brand recognition. Instead of using traditional powder pigments, many manufacturers now prefer this solution to optimize production efficiency and maintain stable color quality.

However, each plastic application requires different performance characteristics, including color dispersion, heat resistance, weather durability and surface appearance. Therefore, choosing and using the right formulation is essential to ensuring high-quality finished products.

What is Color Masterbatch?

Colour Masterbatch is a concentrated mixture of pigments or dyes dispersed in a carrier resin along with processing additives. It is produced in pellet form, making it easy to blend with virgin or recycled plastic materials during manufacturing.  Compared to conventional pigment powders, Color Masterbatch offers several advantages: 
  • Excellent color consistency  
  • Cleaner production process with less dust  
  • Easy dosing and mixing  
  • Improved processing efficiency  
  • Reduced product defects  
  • Better color durability and surface finish  
Today, Color Masterbatch is widely used in plastic processing technologies such as injection molding, blown film extrusion, blow molding, fiber production, and extrusion applications. 

How to Use Color Masterbatch in Plastic Packaging Applications

 

Plastic packaging is one of the largest industries using Color Masterbatch. Different packaging products require different color properties and dosage levels. 
  1. Application in PE Film Blowing
For plastic bags, flexible packaging films, and agricultural films, Color Masterbatch should provide: 
  • Excellent dispersion  
  • No agglomeration  
  • Minimal impact on film strength and transparency  
The typical dosage ranges from 1% to 5%, depending on the desired color intensity. Dark colors such as black, blue, or red often require lower loading levels due to their strong pigmentation.  For outdoor applications, manufacturers are advised to use UV-resistant Color Masterbatch to improve weather resistance and prevent color fading. 
  1. Application in Plastic Bottles and Containers
In HDPE and PET bottle blow molding, Color Masterbatch must withstand high processing temperatures while maintaining stable color performance throughout production.  Important considerations include: 
  • Selecting a compatible carrier resin  
  • Ensuring pigment heat stability  
  • Optimizing dosage to avoid affecting mechanical properties  
For example: 
  • Cosmetic bottles usually require glossy and vibrant colors  
  • Chemical containers often use darker colors for better light protection  

Using Color Masterbatch in Injection Molding 

Injection molding applications demand high-quality surface appearance, uniform coloration, and excellent product finishing. Therefore, selecting premium-quality Color Masterbatch is critical. 
  1. Household Plastic Products
Products such as plastic basins, storage boxes, chairs, and kitchenware often require: 
  • Bright and attractive colors  
  • High gloss  
  • No streaks or uneven coloration  
In these applications, manufacturers should choose Color Masterbatch with superior dispersion and strong compatibility with PP, ABS, or other engineering plastics.  To enhance product aesthetics, many manufacturers also use: 
  • Pearl effect masterbatch  
  • Metallic effect masterbatch  
  • Glitter or shimmer color additives  
  1. Technical Plastic Components
For automotive parts, electronic components, and industrial plastic products, Color Masterbatch must meet additional technical requirements such as: 
  • Heat resistance  
  • UV resistance  
  • Flame retardancy  
  • Chemical resistance  
As a result, masterbatch used in engineering plastic applications generally requires higher technical standards than those used in common household products. 

Color Masterbatch in Fiber and Nonwoven Production 

In PP fiber, PET fiber, and nonwoven fabric manufacturing, Color Masterbatch is used to color fibers directly during production instead of using post-dyeing processes.  This method helps: 
  • Reduce dyeing costs  
  • Minimize wastewater generation  
  • Improve color fastness  
However, fiber applications require Color Masterbatch with: 
  • Uniform pellet size  
  • Excellent dispersion quality  
  • Minimal filter blockage  
Low-quality masterbatch may cause problems such as: 
  • Fiber breakage  
  • Color spots  
  • Uneven coloration  

Important Considerations When Using Color Masterbatch 

To achieve the best production performance, manufacturers should pay attention to the following factors: 
  1. Choose the Right Carrier Resin
The carrier resin should be compatible with the base polymer to ensure optimal dispersion and color adhesion.  Examples include: 
  • PE-based masterbatch for PE film applications  
  • PP-based masterbatch for PP products  
  • PET-based masterbatch for PET bottles  
  1. Control the Dosage Ratio
If the dosage is too low: 
  • The color may appear weak or uneven  
If the dosage is too high: 
  • Production costs increase  
  • Mechanical properties may be negatively affected  
Therefore, trial testing is recommended before mass production. 
  1. Evaluate Heat Resistance
Some pigments cannot tolerate high processing temperatures and may cause: 
  • Color degradation  
  • Discoloration  
  • Loss of gloss  
This is especially important in high-temperature processes such as injection molding and fiber spinning. 
  1. Proper Storage Conditions
Color Masterbatch should be stored: 
  • In dry environments  
  • Away from direct sunlight  
  • Away from excessive humidity  
Improper storage can negatively affect both color quality and processing performance. 

Current Trends in Color Masterbatch Industry 

Today, the market increasingly favors Color Masterbatch products that are: 
  • Environmentally friendly  
  • Free from heavy metals  
  • Compliant with RoHS and REACH standards  
  • Suitable for recycled plastic applications  
In addition, customized color solutions are becoming more popular, especially in packaging, cosmetics, and premium household products.  This trend requires masterbatch suppliers to provide: 
  • Custom color matching services  
  • Stable quality between production batches  
  • Technical support for manufacturers  

Conclusion 

Color Masterbatch plays a crucial role in improving the appearance, performance, and commercial value of plastic products. However, to maximize efficiency, manufacturers must carefully select the appropriate masterbatch type for each specific application and processing technology.  With extensive experience in plastic materials and additive solutions, Mascom Global provides a wide range of high-quality Color Masterbatch products for packaging, injection molding, blow molding, fiber production, and engineering plastic applications. Mascom Global’s solutions are designed to deliver excellent dispersion, color consistency, and compatibility with various polymers, helping manufacturers improve production efficiency and finished product quality.
